As the fool brings the new ass home everyone wants to know how much it cost. He has all publicly assemble and announces just what it cost.

Philosopher gives a penny to a man who throws stones at him but advises him that it will be wiser to throw at one who can afford to give more. The advice is followed and the rascal is arrested and hanged.
Eyes treated for the stomach ache.
A man who has stomach ache from eating bad bread is treated for his eyes so that he will thereafter be able to tell good bread from bad.

A particularly obnoxious man delays others while he haggles over prices with a butcher. Meanwhile a parson takes the three fish the man has laid down and puts them into his large sleeves. The man is angry and searches in vain for them. The parson then shows them and advises him not to let people cheat him.
One wrong and five hundred good deeds.
A man steals a large sum, keeps half and distributes the rest among five hundred persons. He says that he has committed one wrong but has done five hundred good deeds.

Entertained by a lord, they say that they are going to certain waters to recover their appetites. They are taken to a chamber and locked in for a day They recover their appetites without further journeying.
Hungry man eats intestines of fish next morning after refusing to do so the evening before.
The owner of a dog has him given Christian burial. The bishop thereupon pretends that the dog has left the church a large legacy.
The ass absents himself from the parliament of beasts. The lion sends the fox and the wolf to summon him. He pleads his charter of exemption and invites the fox to read it in his hoof.
The stolen meat and the weighed cat.
A man buys three pounds of meat. His wife eats it and says that the cat ate it. The man weighs the cat and finds that it does not weigh three pounds.
The lazy ass repaid in kind.
Loaded with salt, he falls down in the river and lightens his burden. His master then loads him with sponges so that the next time the ass tries the trick he increases his load.
A Jew, fallen into a pit, refuses to be rescued on Saturday, his Sabbath. The next day he calls for help but the Christians refuse to rescue him on Sunday, their Sabbath.

A parson boasts that when he asks his maid if certain work is done she always answers that it has been done long ago. A guest wagers that she can be trapped if she is asked whether she has thrown the parson’s suit of clothes into the tub of water. She overhears the wager and has the suit in the water before he asks the question.
A tenant promises his daughter to his master against her will. The master sends for “that which was promised him.” The daughter sends the horse, and it is taken into the master’s chamber.
Soldiers are admitted neither to hell nor to heaven. They remind Peter of his denial of Christ. He admits them.
A woman tells her brother of God’s omniscience. When he is ill and the priest has been called, he creeps under some straw and hides. The priest leaves.

A guardian of monks in need of food approaches the prince The prince is busy and says that he will permit the guardian but a single word. The guardian says, “Soup”, and secures all the food he wants from the prince.

Two men on parting agree to share everything they receive. One returns with much money. His friend reminds him of the pact. He replies that he has also received many wounds. The friend is willing to forego dividing.
The blacksmith’s and the horse-trader’s dreams.

They are forced to sleep together because of lack of room. The blacksmith tells the horsetrader that he often dreams that he is striking the bellows and that he may accidently strike him in the night. The horsetrader retaliates by dreaming that he is riding a horse and drives the spurs into the blacksmith.
The priest makes the omen come true.

A woman crosses herself when she meets a priest, as if he were the devil. She says that meeting a priest always brings her bad luck. The priest knocks her down and steps on her. “As ye believe, so shall it be.” Pauli (ed.
One king sends large sack of seed to the other to represent the number of his soldiers.
An apprentice harpmaker is blamed that he has not made the harp sound.

A nobleman embezzles money from the public treasury. When counsellors urge an accounting, he replies that he is ready as soon as they have themselves made an accounting of all their transactions. They are ready to let well enough alone.

A traitor is hanged in effigy naked. Later the citizens sue for peace and arrange a meeting. They find him in a hot room swathed with many blankets. He says that he has taken cold when the night wind blew on him as he hung naked from the gallows.
A shoemaker’s apprentice greases boots as he would grease a fowl. The owner in anger returns and breaks a window.

The cobbler learns the minstrel’s songs and sings them so that the minstrel loses his trade. He in turn sews the cobbler’s leather into crazy shapes. He has done no worse than the cobbler, who marred his songs. When they sing together the people realize the contrast and patronize the minstrel.
Brotherly love and patience both dead.

A man failing to receive alms in a village, rings the bell for mass. He tells the sexton that he is ringing because of the death of brotherly love. The sexton rings another bell. It is for the death of the other man’s patience.

In order to test a favorite, a king says that he is going to retire from the world and offers the regency to the favorite. On advice from his philosopher, the favorite says that he is going to accompany the king into retirement.
Robber gives priest double his penance and then takes his horse.
He has a family to support.

Merchant at inn deprives monk of fowl. “It’s against the rules of your order.” Later the monk undertakes to help merchant across stream. In the middle of the stream he asks the merchant if he has any money. “Yes.” The monk drops him in the water.
Priest asked to preach short sermon does so saying to congregation only that they are wicked.
Man asks directions to a certain place. Native attempts to give directions, then in disgust says, “If I wanted to go to
The abbot cannot find his needle.

An undesirable abbot furnishes adequate grounds for his dismissal when he cannot find the needle that all monks are supposed to carry with them. If careless in little things he will be careless in great.
Oracle that the first of three sons to kiss his mother will be king. One of them kisses the earth, mother of all.
Using the lamb to get an audience.
Peasant calls on lawyer for advice. Lawyer says that he is busy. Peasant returns with lamb. The lawyer hears its bleat and grants the audience.
Coins concealed in jar of oil (pickles).
A she-camel has passed, blind in one eye; on the one side she carries wine and on the other vinegar; two men lead her, one a heathen and the other a Jew.
Deduction: the camel ridden by a pregnant woman.
Deduction: the king is a bastard.
After dinner the king begins to dance. He is therefore called illegitimate. His mother acknowledges an intrigue with a dancer.
Deduction: bread made by a sick woman.
It falls apart; therefore it was kneaded by a weak person.
Deduction: mare has she-buffalo as mother.
Deduction: horse has been brought up on ass’s milk.
Deduction: animal has been brought up on dog’s milk.
Can not get enough to eat.
Deduction: prince plays with children because he has been denied a normal youth.
Deduction: one-eyed, long-bearded thief is named Kale Khan.
Banker able to recognize honest merchant by a single hair of his mustache.
Clever deduction of wise man: the theft of a cauldron detected.
Cauldron has been buried in river.
Clever deductions by eating, smelling, drinking, etc.
Person describes approaching bands of warriors without recognizing them.
She saves herself on a tree. The fox, who knows a hundred tricks, is captured.
One basket of wit better than twelve carloads of it.
Female jackal saves herself and husband by quick thinking.
Rainy season or winter (debate between animals).
Makes the horses run by binding a bundle of hay to the shaft.
Penny demanded of every bad man, two pennies of every good man. Thus two pennies received from every man.
Clever ways of attracting the king’s attention.
King’s attention attracted by fighting when it cannot be otherwise gained.
Unjust action brought to inform king of judge’s malfeasance.
Husband is imprisoned and wife detained by judge. She accuses her husband of having stolen her.
Clever ways of breaking bad news to a king, who will kill bearer of bad tidings.
Tidings brought to the king: You said it, not I. The messenger arranges it so that the king says the words in the form of a question.
King’s capriciousness censured: the ass in the stream.

A nobleman seeing an ass letting water in a river remarks that it reminds him of his king. He explains to the king that just as the ass puts water where it is already plentiful, so the king awards wealth where it is not needed. The king says that it is all in the nature of the nobleman’s fate. Subsequent events prove this.
One-eyed king has rocks counted on pain of death.
Clever man avoids saying “one” (which king considers a curse on his one eye) by saying that first is the rock that must not be called by name.
Separates hogs into tenors, bassos, etc. So arranges them that when he pricks them they render a tune.
Poet goes to king to complain of destruction of his dwelling.
King requires story. Poet recites list, ending with account of the destruction of his dun.
Clever hero feigns dullness so as to avenge himself on king.
Son of God to see king.
Two men cannot agree to bride’s dowry. Third party tells each parent that the other has agreed.
Taunts of charioteer to rouse anger in master (who is losing battle) so that he may fight more vigorously.
Poet uses words which student cannot understand and so confounds him.
Extravagant woman whose husband continually finds fault with her.
Sheep, duck, and cock in peril The duck swims; the cock flies to the mast.
Three men greeted by a stranger. Quarrel as to whom he greeted. “I greeted the biggest fool among you.” A contest is held in which tales are told to decide which is the biggest fool.
How he knew she was baking cakes.
Association of wise men with fools.
A wise man follows a fool against his better judgment.
Both are put to death for their foolishness.
The wise man and the rain of fools.
A wise man is persuaded to taste water which has turned many persons into fools. He also becomes a fool.
A wise man refuses to join a foolish crowd who stayed out in an unexpected rain after a long drought. He is punished by them for being a fool.
Forty wise men foretell violent rainstorm.
Failing to convince people, they go into a cave. After the shower they come out. The people call them fools.
Author believes that his book must be stupid.
Stupid people and gossipers are praising it.
Old man silent in king’s presence asks king what he himself does when in company with a fool.
A fool objects to fools as companions.
Leaves when placed between two fools at table.
Three silly pundits sent to a raja as the two-footed cattle he had demanded.
Hero does not learn his name until after first adventure.
The city person ignorant of the farm.
The city girl: Do turnips grow in the ground or on trees?
Unwilling to admit that he does not know what a honeycomb is, a stupid man asks the innkeeper’s wife to roast a slice of honeycomb.
He squeezes the inside out and takes the covering for a sack.
Fool is unacquainted with bananas, throws away the fruit, finds the rest bitter.
Woman is unacquainted with tea, serves the boiled leaves with butter.
The sheep does not understand why the pig being carried to slaughter shrieks.
Urine diagnosis to tell where a man comes from.
A farmer takes some of his master’s urine for examination. The doctor asks where the man comes from.
Fool cannot tell his right hand in the dark.
How to tell the right hand in the dark.
Numskull keeps the candle at his right side as he goes to bed so that he can do so.
Fools do not know what a crayfish is.
Shoot it and build a rampart around it.
Fools do not know what an owl is and attack it.
Unknown animal: a pig captured in a pit.
Foolish lover ignorant of mistress’s flaws.
Foolish lover does not know that his mistress lacks an eye.
Only after his return from an absence does he notice it.
Ignorant priest forces rolls of cloth instead of bread down a dying man’s throat.
Peasants take their old crucifix to an artist for a new one. The artist asks them whether they want a living or dead crucifix.
Numskulls surprised at news that God has a son.
Numskulls surprised to hear that God’s son has died.
Preacher in backwoods asks congregation members who are friends of Jesus to rise.
Backwoods preacher tells couple that they are living in darkness. The woman responds that she has been trying for years to get her husband to cut a window in the house.
Ignorant people told religious holiday is coming the next day: camel appears and is feasted.
Men hide so that God will not see their sin.
Pergamus, a rival city of Luca, objects to the reading of the Evangelium secundum Lucam, insisting that it be “secundum Pergamum”.
“Agnus dei” as a prayer for money.
An ignorant schoolmaster interprets many of the texts of scripture as commands for the priests to live lives of luxury.
Prearranged answers in Latin not always successful.
Stupid scholar memorizes set answers to oral examination in Latin.
The questions are not given in the order he expects; comic results.
The countryman in the great world.
Countryman expects to find persons from his own village when he travels to another land.
His address: a big high house.
Mayor asked about where he lives, names his village and directs the enquirer to a big high house.
Peasants in city inn order whole portion of mustard.
Countryman visiting rich relative in the city refuses to eat dessert: “No, I am not hungry.”
Peasant surprised that king is not larger than other men.
Thinks latrine is kitchen, refuses to take a walk because he fears high houses will fall upon him, etc.
Boy who has never seen a real carpet, hops around the side of the room to avoid stepping on the cloth on the floor.
All sins since the birth of Christ.
Family do not realize that Lent has arrived until it is Palm Sunday.
Then they explain that Lent will be short because it has been a short winter.
Bridegroom does not know what to do on his wedding night.

The numskull groom on his wedding night does not know how to get to the bed, the curtains being drawn. He scales one of the posts, clambers to the canopy, falls upon his bride below, who screams for help.
Fool cannot tell sex of nudes, since they have no clothes on.
Foolish girl ignorant of what is happening at her first menses.
Fool weeps each time he reads a book to see how small letters have become: at school they were big and fat.
Fool asks what he is to talk about when guests arrive.
Absurd ignorance of the use of spectacles.
Fool thinks that “aforesaid” is a title of honor.
Ignorant notary cannot draw up document.
The names of the participants are not the same as those in his sample form.
In the man’s absence eats the mare.
Earthworm thought to be snake (or other monster).
Other animals thought to be a giant cat.
Hero in search of monster brings home a dog, zebra, etc. thinking it is the animal he seeks.
Rabbit thought to be a cow.
Servant sent to bring in cows is found chasing rabbits.
Tiger (lion, etc.) mistaken for domestic animal.
Fool trying to steal goat in dark catches thieving tiger.
Fool rides tiger thinking it to be a big male-goat.
Lion thought to be donkey: drunkard rides it.
Stupid husband mistakes tiger-cubs for jungle cats despite wife’s judgment.
Scotsman thinks moose is a mouse, asks what rats look like in this country.
Hunter mistakes louse on his eyelash for game.
He shoots several times before he notices the trouble.
Numskull thinks fireflies are mosquitoes carrying lanterns to find victims.
Animal or person mistaken for something else.
Sailors light a fire on his back.
Turtle thought to be an island.
White mare thought to be church.
Glowworm thought to be a fire.
The bird who tries to keep the monkeys from this error is killed for her pains.
Fish thought to be chewed sugar-cane.
Numskulls therefore throw away their fish.
Wolf thought to be log of wood.
Bites tiger who tries to play flute.
Snake mistaken for a whip by a blind man.
Living toad or beetles thought to be lost food and therefore eaten by numskulls.
Man mistakes dragon for log, sits on it.
Bear mistaken for a floating log (blanket).
Four blind men feel an elephant’s leg, tail, ear and body, respectively, and conclude it is like a log, a rope, a fan, and something without beginning or end.
Fool mistakes dung-beetles for fruit: eats them.
Animal thought to be a person.
In a ghost house he is thought to be a tailor who snips the devil with his scissors.
Bear on haywagon (on horse) thought to be the preacher.
The bear mistaken for a saint.
The godless man is cheated and attacks a bear thinking it is a saint, and barely escapes with his life.
Crab caught on tiger’s tail thought to be pursuing man.
Deer thought to be man with basket on head.
Dressed up monkey thought to be a nobleman.
The strong man meets a bear in the forest, takes it for a German and struggles with it. Having strangled the bear, fears he has killed a man.
Foolish wife believes goats’ heads are human heads.
Person thought to be an object.
Small priest covered with large hat thought to be a hat.
Sleeping soldier thought to be recumbent statue in chapel.
Horsemen thought to be men mounted on cattle.
Giant thought to be a hill.
Dead man is thought to be alive.
Man with abhorrence for corpse sleeps with one thinking it alive.
Fool lays his hand on demon in the dark, believing it is male goat he has come to steal.
Big tree thought to be snake.
Old sausage (roll) taken for frightening animal.
Object thought to be a turkey.
Island thought to be large dog.
One object thought to be another.
Pumpkin thought to be an ass’s egg.
Numskull thinks he has hatched out an ass’s egg. He thinks that the rabbit which runs out is the colt.
Boy thinks terrapin hatches from bedbug eggs.
Small boy examines bedbug eggs under pillow every morning. One morning he finds a terrapin there.
Potatoes mistaken for “irregular eggs”, or “eggs of the earth.”
Dog mistakes mussel for an egg.
Coins thought to be red beans.
Coins thought to be uncooked cakes.
Culture hero’s pubic hair thought to be bear hair.
Pubic hair of ardent husband’s wife thought to be calf’s tail by peasant in tree.
Man puts food bowl on head thinking it a helmet.
Fish bones in soup thought to be underdone peas.
Fools think evening star is morning star.
Cotton pods knocked off by bullock thought to be lumps of bullock’s fat.
Excrements thought to be meat and therefore eaten.
Gun thought to be clarinet: one man blows, another presses the “keys”.
Foolish tiger thinks dog’s tail is a gun.
Frog thinks cattle are distant country.
Eight-oared ferry-boat mistaken for an animal which must have long legs to wade the stream.
Things thought to be devils, ghosts, etc.
Objects thought to be the devil.
Steamship thought to be the devil.
Watch mistaken for the devil’s eye.
Glowing wheel supposed to be the devil.
Robber or dog in church thought to be a ghost.
Cows in church thought to be ghost.
Dropping dough thought to be a ghost.
It drops on the floor and the man thinks the place is haunted.
Sound of water dripping on dinner pail thought to be ghost using pick in mine.
Noise in house thought to be ghost.
Man sleeping in stable (abandoned cabin) thinks entering animals are ghosts: kills them.
Animal with lighted candle thought to be ghost.
Person in white thought to be ghost.
Sleep-walker thought to be a ghost until discovered.
Person in haunted house shoots off all his toes thinking they are ghosts.
Butter cask thought to be a dead man.
Laughter of boy thought to be spirits’ laughter.
Animals thought to be the devils or ghosts.
Grasshopper thought to be the devil.
Crab thought to be the devil.
Ass thought to be the devil.
Man sees Hereford cow at night; thinks it is devil, says, “Devil I deny thee! I am a psalmsinger and a worshiper of God!” England: Baughman.
Man addresses colt: “Abide, Satan! I am a righteous man and a psalm singer.”
Fool in the dark mistakes cat’s eyes for embers. Is attacked by the cat and he thinks it is the devil.
Fox in coffer thought to be devil.
Black sheep thought to be the devil.
Man thought to be a devil or ghost.
Man costumed as demon thought to be devil; thieves flee.
Woman thought to be devil; thieves flee.
Man mistaken for Famine and Cholera in person.
Priest exorcising demon mistaken for demon and beaten to death.
Man thought to be devil by lion.
Men, on first seeing wives with hair, think they are witches and run away.
Lion thinks man astride him is monster: frightened.
Man reported to be dead so that people flee from him as from a ghost.
Things thought at night to be other frightful object.
Windmill thought to be holy cross (church, God).
Clock ticking thought to be gnawing of mice.
Numskull thinks his shadow is a man pursuing him.
Shadow mistaken for thief: is beaten.
Monkey seeing tiger attack his shadow is frightened so that he falls from tree.
Reflection in water thought to be the original of the thing reflected.
The numskull sees a cow drink from a pool where the moon is reflected. The moon goes under a cloud. He thinks the cow has eaten the moon and slaughters her to recover it.
A numskull sees the moon in the water and throws a rope in to rescue it, but falls in himself. He sees the moon in the sky. At least the moon was saved!
Man (animal) sees moon reflected in water and, thinking it a cheese, dives for it.
Wolf tries to drink well dry to get cheese.
Dogs by river try to get food in river by drinking the river dry.
Demon tries to recover object from river by drinking it dry.
Moon’s reflection thought to be gold in water.
Jackals jump into well after drums and are killed.
Dog drops his meat for the reflection.
Crossing a stream with meat in his mouth he sees his reflection; thinking it another dog with meat he dives for it and loses his meat.
Shooting at enemy’s reflection in water.
Man throws stone at own reflection in water.
Frog leaps into water after elephant’s reflection.
Diving for reflection of beautiful woman.
Woman dives in water three times after reflected image of man peering down from a tree.
Ugly woman sees beautiful woman reflected in water and thinks it is herself.
Ogre sees beautiful woman reflected in water.
Attempts to drink the lake dry.
Man does not recognize his own reflection in the water.
Simpleton thinks his reflection in jar of melted butter is thief; strikes at the jar and breaks it.
Goose dives for star, thinking it a fish.
The next day when she sees fish, she lets it escape.
Fools see bee’s nest reflected in water: try to carry off the well.
Fool sees golden-crested bird reflected in water.
Meantime rascal steals the fruit itself.
Elephant frightened at agitated reflection of moon in water.
Dove sees painted cups of water and dashes into them.
Image in mirror mistaken for picture.
Foolish demon sees his reflection in trickster’s mirror and is convinced he has been captured.
Men build hedge to keep in the moonlight.
Breath in the cold thought to be tobacco smoke.
Words in a foreign language thought to be insults.

Foreigner asks who owns property, clothing, servants; whose wife an attractive woman is; whose funeral is in progress? Answer to each question is “I don’t understand,” which foreigner takes to be a person’s name.
A cleric is asked whether he is of legitimate birth (“de legitimo thoro”).
Conversation by sign language mutually misunderstood.
Similar sounding words mistaken for each other.
Word for wife is similar, so wife is covered.
Daughter says “Sobur” (wait) to her father when he asks what to bring from the journey.
Numskull referring to a forgotten name keeps saying “I have lost it.”
People dive into tank to recover treasure they think he has lost.
A fool given money to buy something to eat; goes around asking for a thing called “something.”
Old woman’s sneeze mistaken for gunfire.
Owl’s hoot misunderstood by lost simpleton.
The old maid answers the owl’s hoot, saying “Anybody, Lord!” or giving the name of the young man she wants.
Turkey’s gobble misunderstood by man lost in woods.
Seeds rattling in pods thought to be insults.
Rabbits think sound of waves is great danger to them.
Hissing of fire thought to be noise of cooking muffins.
Hunchback springs into it to burn to his death.
Numskull thief thinks snoring sleeper is asking for food.
Fool kills his wife because he thinks that she has eaten part of them.
Boiling milk thought to be overflowing.
Numskull thinks his prayers have stopped milk boiling over.
Actually his wife has added cold water.
Boiling pumpkin thought to be talking.
Boiling pot on the floor thought to be self-cooking.
Fish dancing about in cooking pot appears to be many.
Handful of black pepper taken into mouth instead of cooking it in food.
The peasant entertains a priest at tea. Making it, puts in all the tea, six pounds of sugar, a piece of bacon, etc.
Small boy is at home to watch the dinner. Runs into church, calls out to his mother that the sheep’s head has eaten all the dumplings (or butted them out of the pot).
All the beans cooked for one meal.
Stupid servant cooks all the rice for one meal.
Numskull thinks boiling pot is threatening him: breaks pot.
Numskull stays till he has finished.
As he is making water he hears a brook flowing and mistakes what it is. He waits for a day and a half.
Did the calf eat the man?

A fool, liking the shoes on the feet of a man hanged on a gallows, cuts off the swollen feet in order to carry off the shoes. In the room in which he sleeps that night is a newborn calf. The next morning the man takes the shoes but leaves the feet. Peasants agree that the calf has eaten the man all but the feet. They burn the house to destroy the calf.
Fool thinks gold is being destroyed when snails crawl over it.
Fool thinks belly is speaking to him; stabs himself.
Other animals are shouting at him.
Urination of bull thought to be bleeding.
Fools think thorn bush doesn’t sting at night.
Simpleton sleeping in cold room breaks window to let the cold out.
Fool wakes with sleeping mat over head and thinks it is still night.
Peasants go to visit the sea.
Trying to swim in the mist.
Sweeping with a stick instead of a broom.
Misunderstanding of church customs or ceremonies causes inappropriate action.
Christ accused of trying to fool the people.
Fool sees the image of Christ elevated on Ascension Day to the beams of the church. He accuses Christ of having fooled the people into believing that he has gone to heaven.
Christ’s image has broken his arm.

A man refuses to have anything to do with the crucifix because once an image of Christ has fallen on him in church and broken his arm. Reminded that this image is not the same, he replies that it is the son of the other and is just as bad.
Maidservant on way to church on Palm Sunday meets priests leading ass on which Jesus rode. The maid runs home and tells her mistress that the Lord has mounted and has just gone away.
Numskull knocks the figure of Jesus from the ass.
Sees the waving of palms on Palm Sunday and thinks the people are trying to knock the figure from the ass.
Bishop struck for breaking the peace.
At a wedding after a period of silent prayer the bishop begins an antiphony.
Numskull thinks the extinguishing of lights at the church presages a fight.
Move away from Moslem land so that Allah need not be feared.
Numskull refuses communion because his sister died shortly after eating the bread.
Makes ridiculous report to his king.
Christian laws are profitless, Turkish ambassador says.
Good people do not need them; bad people do not reform as a result of them.
The falcon not so good as represented.
A nobleman praises his falcon. His fool, supposing they were praising the falcon as food, kills the bird, but is disappointed in the taste.
A pope in writing to a king says, “To our dear son Frederick.” Upon hearing this the fool cries out, “That is a lie; he is no priest’s son.
A fool sees a boat (with rowers) obedient to commands, “Right!
A landlord in anger throws a dish out the window. The numskull throws the rest out, thinking that the landlord wanted to eat outdoors.
Jumping into the river after their comrade.
Through misunderstanding one of the men jumps into the river. He calls out; the others think that he wants them to follow, and all jump in and are drowned.
Numskull thinks the bishop’s snoring is his death rattle.
He strikes at a fly on the bishop’s nose because it seems to be killing the bishop.
Numskull shoots grasshopper which lighted on the shoulder of his friend and kills friend.
Boy strikes at a fly on his sister’s breast: it turns into nipple and girl thinks it due to brother’s caress.
One man strikes at partridge which has lighted on second man’s head.
Numskulls lose corpse and bury live person instead.
Goat chewing cud angers fool, who thinks goat is mimicking him.
Fool not recognizing coins lying on roadside leaves them.
Man thinks own toe is snake’s head and cuts it off.
Numskull (female devil) thinks her pubic hair has been telling her lies and pulls it out together with the skin.
Fool cannot answer as his mouth is full; thought to have an abscess in cheeks, allows them to be cut open.
Bird protruding from king’s stomach cut out with swords: king killed.
Child’s stomach split open to cure him of wandering.
On the way home from town he destroys his purchases.
Story told about a deer: fool starts chase.
Jackdaw tries to swallow sparks from glowworm.
Numskull strikes all matches in order to try them.
Foolish soldier at guard by cannon therefore quits.
Gift or sale to animal (or object).
Numskull throws money to frogs so that they can count it.
Numskull feeds his wheat to frogs.
He has been sent to mill to have it ground.
Numskull throws money to frogs to repay them.
They have frightened his fleeing ass from the water.
Wool taken to pond for frogs and toads to weave.
Numskulls hear birds calling and give them gifts.
Thankful numskull puts money in the anus of sheep which he supposes has helped him.
When he comes for his money the bird flies to a trash pile, where the fool finds a treasure.
Fool sells balls of thread to great lizard.
Next day he finds a treasure there.
Fool sells goods to a statue.
He is told not to sell to talkative people. The statue is the only one he can find who is not talkative.
Fool sells goods to a statue and when it will not pay him knocks it to pieces. He finds a treasure inside.
An ox strays on the rascal’s land but escapes from him. The next week he sees the ox yoked up and gives him a beating. The master is astonished.
The ass deprived of his saddle.
A man’s coat is stolen when he leaves his ass for a moment. He takes the saddle off the ass and says that he will give it back if the ass will return the coat.
Blamed for not teaching calf better.
Man beats calves because the bull has butted him over the fence.
Wolf punished for his father’s misdeeds.
On a rainy day when shot will not go a man flogs the shot. It goes and he shoots a deer.
In a land where the sickle is not known the new sickle cuts off the head of a man.
Sickle punished by being tied in top of a tree.
The men hang themselves in the attempt.
Man avenges self on animals by wholesale slaughter.
Man avenges brother’s death by wholesale slaughter of wild pigs.
Man punishes offending part of his body.
Man beats his foot for slipping.
Absurd sympathy for animals or objects.
Numskull sees cracks in the ground and feels so sorry for them that he greases them with the butter he is taking home.
Numskull hears limbs creaking in the wind. He is sorry for them and holds them apart. While he is caught between them his enemies take advantage of him.
When the wagon stops its creaking, fool decides it has died; he cremates it.
A numskull climbs a tree to help a cuckoo so that he may call louder than the one in the neighboring forest. Meanwhile his horse is eaten by a wolf.
Fool makes shoes for animals as well as men, since he expects a cold winter.
Cloak given to a stone to keep it warm.
King orders houses built to keep howling jackals warm in winter.
Rider takes the meal-sack on his shoulder to relieve the ass of his burden.
Man puts bag of meal on one side of saddle, balances it on the other side with a rock.
A fool eats nuts. A kernel slips from him.
The woman thinks the boiling pot is complaining.
Numskulls try to take home a wave of the sea in a bamboo rod. At home when it refuses to wave they say that it is homesick for its mother, the sea.
Numskull thinks money piece covered with perspiration after he has held it for awhile is weeping.
Absurd sympathy for animals or objects—miscellaneous.
Men drag carts on to roof to shade it from the sun.
Animals or objects treated as if human—miscellaneous.
Animal or object expected to go alone.
Object sent to go by itself.
Cheeses thrown down to find their way home.
Numskull lets one roll down hill; sends the other to bring it back.
Three-legged pot sent to walk home.
Table thrown out of the sledge; to go home by itself.
Spinning wheel is sent home by itself.
The man asks his wife if it has arrived before him, finds that it has not. “I thought not.
Sickle laid in field and told to cut grain.
Fool sends letter home by a flooded river.
Animal sent to go by itself.
Ass loaded and commanded to go home.
Since he is a swift runner they expect it to reach the landlord in time.
Fishes to stop at his house.
Fool directs them as he places them in stream.
Fool believes they can be taught.
Fool made to believe that his ass (ox) has been educated and has become mayor.
Trickster joins bulrushes in a dance.
He thinks they are dancing when he sees them waving.
Simpleton addresses a field of reeds.
The woman tries to tire out her rival’s boat so as to win the race, but only tires herself.
A boy roasts snails and they make noise in cooking.
Fool puts black clothes on his hen’s necks. He tells people that they mourn their mother.
Fools chain a wheelbarrow, bitten by a mad dog, lest it bite others.
Wants the organ to come and play for her.
An old woman enraptured with the sound of a cathedral organ prays for it to come to her house and gives it directions as to where she lives.
A man has drunk so much of various wines that he is sick.
On his deathbed refuses to forgive nails which ruined his tools.
Sea says that it is calm itself, but the wind blew it up and broke the ship.
A boy recently home from school sees his mother trying to catch the cock. “Don’t mother, don’t break his freedom or we will suffer for it.” Pauli (ed.
Scholar speaks Latin on hunt so that the birds cannot understand him.
Woman thinks calf’s bleating has accused her of stealing from harvest.
Begs that people not believe what calf said.
Objects supposed to be born, grow, and die like animals.
Absurd disregard or ignorance of animal’s nature or habits.
Absurd ignorance concerning the laying of eggs.
A woman wants her hen to lay many eggs. Overfeeds her and she stops laying altogether.
Numskull feeds hens hot water so they will lay boiled eggs.
Absurd ignorance concerning the hatching of eggs.
Numskull sits on eggs to finish the hatching.
Cautions people to be quiet and not frighten the eggs.
Numskull tries to hatch out a calf from a cheese.
Absurd ignorance concerning animal’s eating and drinking.
The water on the calf’s back.
When the calf will not drink, the peasant woman throws the water on its back.
When the customer refuses to take the milk he puts it back into the goat’s mouth so that it will flow back into the udder.
A farmer who wanted to fatten a pig fed it only twice a day.
How can an elephant eat, having tails at both ends?
Absurd ignorance concerning place for animal to be kept.
Cow (hog) taken to roof to graze.
Fools build an enclosure to keep in the cuckoo. She flies over the hedge. They say that they have not built the hedge high enough.
Fools try to hedge the cuckoo so that they will have summer the year round (the coming of the first cuckoo being the sign of the coming summer).
Deer belled and enclosed like goats jump fence and escape.
Hogs made to sleep in trees to cure their filthy habits.
Nest built in tree for fish.
Fish will climb trees like buffaloes.
Numskull considers what will happen if river burns up.
Fool does not milk cow for a month so that she will give plenty for a feast.
Fools try to milk male ass.
The brother who owns the front end tries to drive the cow and will not let the owner of the rear end milk her.
Fool asks owner of oxen why he does not milk them since he is not working them.
Trying to have cows make curds before being milked.
Cow killed in order to get all the milk at once.
Bullock struck on hindquarters instead of head in attempt to kill it.
Absurd attempt to change animal nature.
A man has a cat trained to hold up lighted candles on its head. The king has a mouse let loose. The cat drops the candle and chases the mouse.
Cat transformed to maiden runs after mouse.
Absurd disregard of animal’s nature or habits—miscellaneous.
Fisherman fails to make fish dance to his flute.
Later in his net they jump about without the aid of the flute.
Fool tries to shoot dead antelope until it will come to him.
Numskull tries to shake birds from tree like fruit.
Breeding fine horses from an ass.
Fool says, “Just as soon as the body of a colt bred from this mare is in proper proportion to its ears you will have a fine horse.” Pauli (ed.
Sheep licking her lamb is envied by the wolf.
Numskull tries to wash black hen white.
Fear that frog may drown or get dirty.
Numskull does not understand about baby’s skull.
Foolish mother does not understand how babies cry.
Horse taught to live without food.
Three brothers take turns using mule.
None of them feeds him, supposing that the others have. The mule dies.
Fool carries wife across stream head downwards and drowns her.
A trickster cuts off the bill and legs of a stork to make him look more like a real bird.
A fool is asked where the river is fordable. He says, “Everywhere.” The man tries to ride across and is almost drowned.
Fool cuts off tails of oxen so that they will look like fine steeds.
Ignorant bride castrates groom when jokingly told to do so.
Nun tells friar to get rid of offending member.
Fool undergoes castration to put on weight.
Simpleton’s ignorance of anatomy leads him to share his wife with a priest.
Fool believes that he has begot child with his sister by an earbox.
The man without a member: foolish wife gives her husband money to buy himself one.
Cowboy shoots his wife when she breaks her leg (or is injured in another way).
The needle (or the like) falls into the sea: sought the next summer.
Marking the place on the boat.
An object falls into the sea from a boat. Numskulls mark the place on the boat-rail to indicate where it fell.
Marking the place under the cloud.
Numskulls leave a knife in the field, marking the place by putting it under a heavy cloud. Next day the cloud is gone and the knife lost.
Fool seeks the ears of grain in the direction of the cloud toward which he has sowed them.
Marking the place in the sand.
Vessel left under mound in sand while owner is swimming. Others make similar mounds so that it is lost.
Numskull looks for bread that he threw away a year before.
Numskull forgets name of certain food and thinks that it has fallen into sand.
Money tested by throwing it into a stream to see if it will swim.
Good coins are supposed to swim, counterfeit to sink.
Sowing cheese to bring forth a cow.
Planting a hog in order to grow pigs.
Planting animal’s tail in order to produce young animals.
Harvesting early for half a crop.
Stones watered to make them grow.
Numskull tries to dig up a well (spring).
He wants to take it home.
A hole to throw the earth in.
Numskull plans to dig a hole so as to have a place to throw the earth from his excavation.
A peasant hangs boots and an accompanying letter on a telegraph wire, expecting them to reach the city.
How he looks in his sleep.
Man takes mirror to bed to see whether he sleeps with his mouth open.
Dead man identified by his cough.
Numskull asked to identify corpse tries to do so by his cough.
A healthy place for a tomb.
Numskull objects to unhealthy place for his tomb.
They put meal in the boiling current of the ice hole and then, one after another, they jump in to taste the porridge.
How far his voice will reach.
A numskull ties yarn around the stove to keep the heat from escaping.
Numskull tries to find the time of night.
Sundial covered in order to protect it.
Trying to get fruit from fruitless tree.
Numskulls try to get pears from an oaktree.
They accuse each other of eating all the pears.
Numskull stretches out his hands toward the fire across the river.
As tired as if he had walked.
So says the numskull after riding to town on his stick horse.
Fire and water mixed to make sacrifice.
Fool told that he needed only the two.
Demand that murderer restore life to victim.
Woman runs after guest to tell him he must restore her husband whom he has unintentionally killed.
Simpleton drives goats into a well, because he thinks it would be cooler for them.
Hot sickle put into water to cure its fever.
Fool loses his mother’s corpse on way to funeral. Mistakes old woman for mother and substitutes her.
White sheep-skin used as a source of light.
Trying to catch light in a mouse-trap.
An old woman who has forgotten to knead it in the dough throws it into the stove.
The fool puts but one stick of wood in the stove.
Tree-trunks laid crosswise of the sledge.
In a storm on the ice, numskulls stick needles into the ice to keep from blowing away.
But the man who uses the crowbar is to blame for the downfall of the wall.
He comes to a stream but not wishing to get his feet wet he sits down to wait for the stream to run down. He helps to bale the stream out with a hazelnut shell and keeps it up for months.
Fools try to use buffalo tongue as a knife.
Stupid woman swims on the roof.
Tree pulled down in order to give it water to drink.
Fool tries to purify cotton by burning it (as the goldsmith does with gold).
Numskulls are affected by heat from stove which has no fire in it.
Mouth and ears stopped up lest wisdom escape.
Numskull’s beard cut off: does not know himself.
Woman’s garments cut off: does not know herself.
Woman in tar and feathers does not know herself.
Fool in new clothes does not know himself.
Man does not know himself from another identically clad.
Fool at baths believes he is someone else.
Sees everybody naked. Puts straw on his shoulder to identify himself. Straw floats to another bather.
Man made to believe that he is someone else.
White man made to believe that he is a negro.
Sleeps with a negro. His friends blacken him during the night. When he is waked up, he complains that they have waked the wrong man.
Man made to believe that he is a dog.
A numskull ties a pumpkin to his leg at night so that he shall know himself in the morning. Someone ties the pumpkin to another’s leg and the numskull is not sure of his identity next morning.
Numskull made to believe he is an evil spirit.
Fool does not recognize his own house and family.
His pupils grab a dog’s tail and think it is their master’s.
Man does not recognize his name when it is called: he is accustomed to hear his nickname.
Inability to find own members, etc.
Numskulls cannot find their own legs.
A stranger helps them with a switch.
Numskull asks doctor which leg (own) is hurting him.
Numskull cannot find ass he is sitting on.
Numskull doesn’t recognize his own horse.
Finds it only when the rest ride away and he takes the only one left.
Inability to find object one is carrying.
Man searches for axe which he carries on his shoulder.
Woman cannot find pastry which is sticking to her posterior.
Fools try to fight with man inside of drum who seems to make the noise.
Opium-smoker on journey asks his way about; ends up at his own house.
Counting wrong by not counting oneself.
Numskulls conclude that one of their number is drowned.
Numskulls count selves by sticking their noses in the sand.
There are ten horses; then when he is mounted there are only nine.
Culture hero throws coconuts to various islands, but forgets one he stands on: hence none now on that island.
Are there nine or ten geese?
Ten men are called in; each is to take a goose. If all have a goose, there are ten. One man is left without one.
Three girls distressed by seemingly impossible task of going and returning together—one in half month, other in fifteen days, other in seven plus eight days.
While the merchant is making calculations, he asks the age of his youngest daughter, the elder daughter, and the mother, and always adds this to the number he has reached.
Keeping the measure by stretching out the arms.
Numskull goes to buy goods for his wife.
Numskulls buy things in common: each pays full price.
Numskulls buy church in common: each pays full price.
Three brothers buy cow for common use; each brother pays the farmer full price.
Actor forgets and speaks in his own person.
In Passion Play the Christ says, “I am thirsty”; the thief on the left speaks up, “I too.”
As result of his absent-mindedness he is given a heavy mortar to take to his master. The latter makes him return it as punishment.
Fool believes plea of not guilty even though he has seen man injure him.
Hero keeps on leading his horse without discovering that it is dead.
Given things for self and relatives, fool forgets to take his own.
Wise man short-sightedly scorned for his advice.
God’s mercy contrasted with man’s short-sightedness.
Quarrel and fight over details of air-castles.
Man plants hedge: sheep will leave wool on the thorns and bring riches.
To build a palace in the sky: hawk as architect is let fly in the air.
Fools cast lots for royal purple of queen who is still alive.
Air-castle shattered by lack of forethought.
Air-castle: the jar of honey to be sold.
In his excitement he breaks the jar.
Air-castle: basket of glassware to be sold.
In his excitement he breaks the glassware.
Air-castle: basket of eggs to be sold.
In her excitement she breaks all the eggs.
Pot of flour to be sold: broken.
Air-castle: jar of oil to be sold.
Air-castle: pail of milk to be sold.
Proud milkmaid tosses her head (or kicks the pail in her sleep) and spills the milk.
Air-castles: pail of milk to be sold.
Old woman thinks about the horse she is finally to get from the sale. In her imagination she spurs it and spills the milk.
Air-castle: to sell hide of sleeping deer.
In his excitement he wakes the deer, who runs off.
Toad having found money daydreams and is run over.
Which way the sheep shall return.

One man plans to buy sheep; another says that he shall not drive them across the bridge. They quarrel over the sheep, which have not yet been acquired. A third numskull to convince them of their foolishness pours all his meal out in the water so as to show them the empty sack. “How much meal is in the sack?” he asks.
Foolish logician upsets ghee in argument.
Distress over imagined troubles of unborn child.

(Clever Else.) Girl sent to cellar to get wine to serve the suitor begins weeping over the troubles of the child which she might have if she married the suitor. Her parents join her. Meanwhile the suitor leaves.
Queen grieves herself to death over fate of her children after her death.
Servant plans to deceive his master by refusing to eat.
The hungry fox waits in vain for horse’s scrotum (lips) to fall off.
The daw waits in vain for the figs to ripen in winter.
Men (animals) wait in vain for nuts to fall from a tree.
Waiting in vain for fruit to fall from a non-fruitbearing tree.
Wolf scorns salt meat (etc.) in false expectation of other booty.
Wolf waits in vain for the nurse to throw away the child.
She has threatened to throw the child to the wolf.
Dog waits to be hit with meat.
A butcher has threatened to hit him with a piece of meat.
Dog follows washerwoman with bundle hoping for meat.
Dupe waits for rear wheels of wagon to overtake front wheels.
Is told that money is thus made.
Hare waits in vain for leaves to fall from palm tree.
Hare waits in vain for man’s hand to fall off.
Sacrifice of one son to get another.
A woman plans to sacrifice her only son so that the gods will permit her to give birth to another son.
Short-sighted wish: grain to grow without beards.
Short-sighted wish: all he pulls on will follow.
He blows his nose and it pulls out long.

The man complains that he is a mere slave of his stomach. His wish is granted and the stomach taken away from him. He discovers soon that life has become very uninteresting to him, and recovers his stomach again.
Short-sighted wish: camel wishes a long neck.
Old woman demands something that she would remember all her life: her nose cut off.
Same wishes used wisely and foolishly.
Given to two persons with opposite results.
Wise and foolish wish: keep doing all day what you begin.
One begins pulling linen out of a box; other in anger begins throwing water on the pig and must do so all day.
Wise and foolish wish: help in whatever one is doing.
One gets help in work, other in striking his wife (etc.).
Twice the wish to the enemy.
(The covetous and the envious). A can have a wish, but B will get twice the wish. A wishes that he may lose an eye, so that B may be blind.
A husband, given three wishes, transfers one to his wife, who wastes it on a trifle; in his anger he wishes the article in her body and must use the third to get it out.
Transferred wish wisely used as well as unwisely.
Two transferred wishes used unwisely: redeemed by wise use of third.
Wife uses two transferred wishes selfishly. Husband kills wife and uses remaining wish to his advantage.
Woman disdainfully throws away pills; punished with sores on body, must use the pills to restore herself.
Wife granted wish for beauty, elopes with prince.
Husband wishes her into a pig; son must use third wish to restore her.
Granted any wish, the fool chooses a trifle.
Absurdly modest wish: no lights on certain night except in her own house.
Wife wishes to be turned to gold.
Foolish wish: to destroy all flies and spiders.
Foolish bargain: horse for cow, cow for hog, etc.
Foolish bargain: good fish for worthless shell; shell with pearl in it for small fish.
Fool exchanges his wife with ox; thinks something to be wrong with her head (she has been marked with red at the parting of her hair).
Fools sent to buy cow procure a monkey instead.
Squaring accounts by shaving the wife.
A numskull has paid twice the regular amount for a shave. The barber shaves the wife.
The foolish attempt to cheat the buyer.
One-third for the price of one-fourth.
In the grain sale the fool sells a third of a cask for the price of a fourth, thinking that he is cheating the buyer.
Two for the price of one.
The fool sells two fox-skins pulled into each other.
Seller of fox skins mixes otter skins with them.
Ten for the price of nine.
A fool buys nine eggs and sells ten for the same price. He says that business is improving.
A heaping measure given for a level measure.
Selling more yards of goods for the money than they received.
Lost ass, saddle, and bridle offered as reward to the finder.
Man trades his only horse for a set of harness.
The woman sells cows and gets one of them back as a pledge for the unpaid purchase price.
The auctioneer praises the man’s worthless cow so much in his speech that the man takes her back himself.
A numskull having an over-short turban for sale at auction warns the prospective buyer that it is too short.
The fool advises the buyer that the horse is worth little or his father would not sell it.
Seller advises buyer that cow is a thief.
Thief warned what not to steal.
The numskull tells the thief where his door-key, his cakes, and his roasts are and warns him not to steal them.
Fool hides treasure and leaves sign “Here it is.”
Thief leaves sign “Here it is not.” Pauli (ed.
A man finds a treasure, but is robbed by porters whom he has employed to rid him of the trouble of carrying it.
Valuables given away or sold for trifle.
Numskull gives away the old water bag in which the money is hid.
Woman gives a jewel for a salad.
The recipient is also a numskull and doesn’t know its value.
Fool ignorant of value of jewel throws it away.
Boy refuses pearls for worthless stones; jeweler recognizes them for what they are.
Good timber given for useless because wife says they will have only sickness and trouble.
Sacks of gold and silver traded for sacks of rice.
Gold and jewels sold for trifle.
Expensive wood burned to make charcoal.
Stupid boy convinced that trading all his silver for worthless cup will gain people’s respect.
Woman exchanges a horse for a sack of bones.
She has been falsely told that the sack is filled with gold.
In a land in which cats are not known, one is bought at a great price. It eats many mice. By misunderstanding, they think the cat is a monster. In order to get rid of it they set the house on fire.
Woman wishing to punish a cat fastens cotton to its tail and lights it. The whole village is burnt.
Expensive means of being rid of insects.
Sleeping in shoes to avoid insect bites.
Snake rids himself of wasps: he lets himself be run over by a cart wheel along with them.
Bald man aims at a fly: hurts his head.
House burned down to rid it of insects.
House burned down to get rid of lizard.
The house catches fire and burns.
Clothes burned to rid them of insects.
Crop burned to rid it of insects.
Frogs to eat insects, snakes to eat frogs.
The cat to guard the cheese.
A farmer troubled with mice eating his cheese places a cat in the tub with the cheese. She eats the mice and the cheese.
Woman puts cat in flour bin to catch a mouse. The cat eats the pie in the bin and loses interest in the mouse.
Pursuing the rabbit who harmed the garden.
Peasant asks a nobleman’s help against a rabbit. The nobleman chases the rabbit on horseback for five days and ruins the peasant’s crop.
King ruins his garden to get rid of viper.
House burned down to get rid of rats.
When it gives too much heat numskulls decide to move it instead of putting out the fire.
Cleaning the church by moving it.
A cow fouls a church. Numskulls try to move the church with ropes.
To keep croaking frogs from disturbing him, the fools shoot at the frogs all night.
Man kills self to make quarrelsome wife a widow.
Taming the bull by cutting off his horns.
It makes him the more violent.
Punishing the dog by feeding him.
A man is bitten by a dog. On the advice of an old woman he rubs bread on the wound and gives it to the dog. All dogs will bite him if they thus get double reward.
Gray hair cured by pulling it out so that the person is bald.
Young wife pulls out his gray hairs; old wife his black.
Getting the calf’s head out of the pot.
A calf gets its head caught in a pot. A fool cuts off the calf’s head and then breaks the pot to get it out.
Man strikes off donkey’s head to punish it.
Snakes in pond to be killed: eels also killed.
Fools take fatal overdose of medicine.
Nose cut off to get it out of the light.
Improving the wife’s face by cutting off her nose.
One contestant chooses straight path through stones; other circles about and wins.
Noodles push parents over a rock as a favor to them.
Numskulls bore hole in boat in order to make water run out.
Stupid giant, seeing how fat he has become, wants to eat himself up.
Boy has rice in joined hands and arms around a pillar. Afraid to move lest rice be lost. Roof is removed and boy lifted over pillar.
Stupid cowherds apply hot iron to temples of unconscious man to revive him.
Cow tied tight with stones in order not to blow away, but is unable to do all others things too.
Hero beheads old woman who asks him to cure her of old age.
Disregard of danger to objects (or animals).
Candle put in the stove to dry: melts.
Sunlight carried into windowless house in baskets.
When this plan does not succeed, they gradually pull down the house to get light.
Putting the fish aside for Easter.
They are put in one big pool, but an eel eats them up.
Numskull sends meat home through kite (bird); kite devours it.
Numskull ties their beaks and weights them down in the river with stones.
Numskull to water roots of tree.
Digs up the tree to find the roots.
Trees cut down to gather fruit.
Numskull is to carry a can of oil with especial care since it has a little hole in it. In order to find the hole he turns the can about and lets all the oil run out.
Disregard of danger to objects or animals—miscellaneous.
Fools make a boat go over a precipice.
Quarreling heirs destroy the entire property involved.
Getting all the eggs at once.
A peasant kills his hen so that he can immediately get all the eggs she will lay during the next year.
He has been told to stick it in his sleeve.
Numskulls take out the clothing and cover the trunks to keep rain off.
Horse drawn across ice till skin is rubbed off.
Fool sows his mother’s seed rice on other people’s fields.
Numskulls try to kill mosquitoes with bows and arrows: only injure themselves.
Numskull tries to preach while the priest is preaching: beaten.
Bees caught in sack which is opened at home.
Girl hacks off her heel to get shoe on.
Fool cuts off his arms to wear sleeveless sweater.
Dupe persuaded to cut off part of his own body.
Man lays piece of wood on his leg to saw it: saws leg off.
Trickster puts on buffalo skull: gets head caught.
Numskull licks out pot: gets it caught on his head.
Numskull sticks his head in the branches of a tree.
Numskull sticks his head into the hole of a millstone.
Wolf trying to catch tongue of camel puts head in camel’s mouth: killed.
Jackal’s head caught in pot of blue dye.
Animals make him king, but detect him from his cry and turn him out.
Sticks his head into it and gets drowned himself.
Man catches buffalo by rope and is dragged to death.
Numskull ties the rope to his leg as the cow grazes on the roof.
The cow falls off and the man is pulled up the chimney.
Fool ties rope to his leg and to dog.
Hand bound to dog’s leash: person dragged.
Milker ties cow’s tail to himself.
Jackal ties captive crow to his tail.
Crow pecks self loose and injures jackal’s tail.
Animal allows himself to be tied to another’s tail and is dragged to death.
Other animal’s tail tied to tiger’s (leopard’s): killed when tiger flees.
Camel with ass on his back dances.
Monkey jumps over a ravine with his sword girded on.
Cat crawls to steeple and tries to fly.
Coyote attempts to fly from a treetop: falls.
Numskull cuts off tree-limb on which he sits.
Men hang down in a chain until top man spits on his hands.
Wife carried up tree to sky in bag in husband’s teeth.
She asks question and he drops her when he answers.
Servant carrying master across stream answers question with gesture that throws master off.
Numskull going to heaven holding on tail of divine elephant, looses his hold to make gesture.
He and all holding on to him fall.
Three men in a tree sing song and clap hands: they fall down and die.
Wolves climb on top of one another to tree: lowest runs away and all fall.
Measuring the tower by piling up hampers.
They place hampers on top of one another. The fool has them take out the two on the bottom.
Intruding wolf falls down chimney and kills himself.
Blind leading blind falls into pit.
Monkey jumps into water after a butterfly.
Hedgehog and crab jump from boat after turtle.
Woman tries to climb rope of excrement and urine.
Fool dangling from tree by hands tries to clap them together: falls.
Falls and injures self and others.
How was the pigeon killed? Fool aims stone at inquirer saying, “I struck him like this.”
Trickster eats medicines that physic him.
Numskulls eat medicine that physics them.
Biscayans pour medicine into rice for broth with which to cook rice.
Numskull having enough food to last him eleven out of the twelve months fasts the entire first month so as to get the ordeal over. He starves with eleven months’ supply on hand.
Numskull brings about his own capture.
Coyote wears fox’s rattle; caught in brush and injured.
Trickster gets caught on a fishhook.
Goat eats in garden and is caught.
Thief stops to admire beautiful things before stealing them.
Thief debates whether to take one thing or another.
Thief of deer cuts it up and keeps counting pieces.
Numskull as thief’s assistant wakens owner.
Pleads successfully that he was trying to awaken the household and prevent theft.
Foolish thief cooks food and awakens household.
Foolish thief asks help of owner.
Master asked to help in the theft.
The fool sent in by thieves is told to bring out the heaviest thing. As this is a grain-grinder and he cannot carry it, he wakes the master of the house to help him.
Thieving numskull beats drum (blows trumpet, etc.) he finds in outhouse.
Thieves disposed of one at a time.
They will not help each other since the fewer thieves there are the more there is to share.
Greedy jackal caught in carcass of dead bullock.
The flea bites the man and jumps away. The bed is searched and the louse killed.
Dogs of wolf color join the wolves.
As soon as they have killed the other dogs the wolves then turn on the wolf-colored dogs which they have persuaded to join them.
Bee rests on water lily which closes over it at night and kills it.
Crocodile swallows water-snake, which kills him.
Sheep killed by the butcher, who they are persuaded will spare them.
Camel and ass together captured because of ass’s singing.
King attempts to visit the spirit world underground and dies in a tunnel.
Foolish interference in quarrel of the strong fatal to the weak.
Sparrow intervenes in quarrel between elephants: crushed to death.
Disastrous jump to retrieve lost object.
Miser jumps into a ravine to retrieve single grain.
Man leaps into river and drowns in effort to save his treasure.
Trying to draw both legs on at once.
The shirt is sewed together at the neck. The man’s head is cut off so that the shirt can be put on him.
Burning the temple to attain notoriety.
Fool whose house is burning puts wood on the fire.
People row to land and fetch water from a spring to put out the fire.
Carrying the plow horse so as not to tramp up the field.
Numskulls carry one another through mud and the others back in order that not all get dirty.
Sedan-bearers must carry master about searching for dog since they have refused to search.
Rowing in a boat which is tied up.
Carrying load up hill to roll it down.
Fools carry log (millstone) down hill. They realize that they might have rolled it down. They therefore carry it back up hill to roll it down.
Short-sighted lover is slow to follow up advantage.
The porridge in one, the milk in another.
In preparation, the feet are cut off the evening before.
Ship built with a wooden saw.
The ship has no bottom and is so narrow that nothing can get into it.
The ogre tars the hero’s boat, thinking to injure him.
Attempts to make canoe of sand.
Does not need roof when it is fair; cannot put it on when it rains.
Fool roofs his house on the inside.
Builders throw away beams from the scaffolding until it all falls down.
The first lets his axe fall. The others throw theirs in the same place.
Bird nest of salt melts away.
Man on camel has doorway broken down so he can ride in.
It does not occur to him to dismount.
The shepherd who cried “Wolf!” too often.
When the wolf really comes no one believes him.
Shepherd shuts up the lion in the yard with the live-stock.
He hopes to capture the lion, but loses all his beasts.
Wolf almost locked up in the stable by the shepherd.
Wolf locked up with the sheep.
Before eating his booty the numskull sleeps.
Getting a sword to lift the cheese.

A numskull sees a cheese by the side of the road and tries to lift it up with his sword, but the sword is too short. He leaves the cheese and goes away to borrow a longer sword. Meantime someone else takes the cheese.
The bird boasts about capturing the rabbit.
Meantime other birds eat the rabbit.
A fool in celebration of the capture of a deer puts his clothes on the bound deer. He throws a knife to cut the deer’s throat but the knife cuts the snare and the deer runs away with the clothes.
Fool kills chickens by throwing them off a balcony against a stone.
Crocodile goes after the second child.
He finds two children bathing in the river and carries one to his hole. He tells the child to wait while he goes for the other child. Both children escape.
Trickster travels while fish cook: they burn up.
Man saves trouble by milking cow directly into his mouth.
How to remove hairs from salt.
Washed with water, salt melts away.
His last request: a red cap.
A man about to be hanged keeps asking for his red cap which he has left in prison. He has no thought of his real peril.
Wholesome food for the day of hanging.
A man about to be hanged is very particular about his bread lest it impair his health.
Having the head dressed before hanging.
A man who has hurt his head in trying to hang himself has the head dressed by a doctor and then goes and hangs himself.
Hang me right away so I can get back to work.
A schoolmaster whips his pupils to keep them from wrong-doing. He does not wait until after the deed is done.
Priest beats wife before purchasing food since he wishes her to cook it in particular way.
Scolding the drowning child instead of helping him.
Absent-minded nurse lets child down into well instead of bucket.
Man lets his infant son play in river.
Numskull is sent to fetch children.
He either smothers them during conveyance or scalds them during bathing.
Numskull kills his children trying to cure their illness.
Fool lets wine run in the cellar.
He (she) falls into a study (or chases a dog) while the spigot is open.
Fool tries to dry up spilt wine with meal.
Drinking gruel by making hole in pot.
No room left for the feast.
A peasant on the way to a feast drinks so much ditch-water that he has no room left for the feast.
Master sets servant example by eating rind first: fills up and never reaches the fruit.
Numskulls buy a charter from their lord. In celebration they get drunk and use the seal as a candle and forfeit their charter.
A fleeing fox loses an eye in the briars.
Returns the next day and eats it, thinking that it tastes like chicken.
The dog between the two castles.

In castles on opposite hills guards play different tunes during meals. The dog goes toward the music in one castle but when he is about half way up the hill the music begins on the other. He keeps alternating and running up and down until the meals are over and he gets nothing.
Bird overcareful about food suitable to its color is killed by eagle.
Two prisoners use up their hour of grace disputing over road to take home.
Princess who is too choosy finally marries an idiot.
Whose duty to put out fire?
Officers investigate; meanwhile fire burns town.

A Brahmin washes clothes to purify them. As they hang to dry, a dog walks under them and the Brahmin fears that they are polluted. By putting himself on all-fours like a dog and fastening a leaf like a dog’s tail he experiments and decides that the dog must have touched the clothes. He therefore destroys them instead of rewashing them.
A foolish priest is pushed into the water.
“If you had hanged me you would have really been in trouble.”
A trickster creates men from his excrements (or the like). They melt in the sun.
The bear riding the horse lets his paws fall on the horse’s flanks.
He is caught on a tree and leaves his claws in the horse’s flesh.
The man who wanted to be dead one day.

A husband tells his wife that he has provisions for every day in the year but one. He proposes to play dead for that one day, thinking that the servants will be overcome with grief and cannot eat. After brief mourning, however, they eat more than usual. The man then thinks to frighten them by rising from the dead. One servant thinking the dead man suffering from devils kills him.
A fool releases a bear while the master is away.
The bear plays havoc. The master threatens to cut off the ears of the meddler. The fool asks his dog not to tell on him.

A fool is told that he is to go to a neighboring castle the next morning. He is to take letters, but the next morning without reporting for instructions the fool goes on the journey. He is given a bag of stones to carry back.
A fool is sent to tell his master’s wife that he will not return that day for dinner. He delays the message for a week.
Fool has himself buried because he stinks.
Raven steals the robes of Red Willow Men and finds them useless.
People pelt each other with food.
An abbot is planning to build a palace.
Bewailing a calamity that has not occurred.
Fool rings bell to announce that he has won at chess.
No one comes when he rings to save his home from fire.
Woman to sound bell for help in childbirth persuaded to sound false alarms: not heeded when help is needed.
Persons build a wheelbarrow too large to come out of shed.
Nine men try to lift bull over the fence.
One gets the idea of taking it through the gate.
Numskull is glad to hurt his feet instead of his shoes.
Logical absurdity based upon certain false assumptions.
Frogs reprove ass for lamenting when he falls into morass.
A magpie is punished by his master, who throws him into a mud puddle. The magpie sees a muddy sow. He says, “You also must have had a quarrel with your master.” Pauli (ed.
Dogs flee from their master because in time of famine he has killed his cattle. If he kills the cattle, he will surely kill the dogs.
Ass brays on hearing a conch shell.
Owner thinks he must have been a saint in a former life.
Effects of age and size absurdly applied.
Two fifteen-year old slaves ordered: fool brings one thirty years old.
Priest to have maid at least fifty years old: gets one aged twenty and one aged thirty.
Burial in old grave to deceive angel.
Fool thinks that the angel who comes to question him will pass him by since he has apparently been dead a long time.
Wooden anchor would hold if it were only large, thinks the fool.
The reef is old, the ship new.
They think the vessel will endure the shocks better than the reef.
A numskull who rides an ox to a tournament is ridiculed. He says, “He is swifter than a horse.
The Zodiac grows up: the Kid becomes the Goat.
A fool who was born under the sign of the Kid declares that he was born under the Goat.
Boat expected to grow into ship.
Peasant no longer wants a horse since the new born foal is so heavy to carry.
Our children know local road; odd that grown stranger does not.
Each of two persons wants to sleep in the middle.
A profitable fight: three for one! A priest boasts of his profitable fight with the peasants, where he has received three blows for every one given.
Fool regrets that he had not eaten number seven first since that was the one that brought satisfaction.
If the horse can pull one load he can pull two.
A numskull is asked how many daily prayers (Moslem) there are.
Numskull asked the number of commandments replies that there are twenty. He explains to another that he knows there must be more than twenty because the minister would not accept his answer.
Selling his half of the house.
A man owns half a house. He wants to sell his half so as to get money to buy the other half and thus have a whole house.
Dentist duped to pull out two teeth for one because of the expensiveness.
Man prefers small oysters, since he will get more to the hundred.
Numskull finds that one feather makes a hard pillow, thinks a sackful would be unbearable.
Absurd generalization from a particular incident.
Fool warns those who ride through a field of peas. “You will burn your horses’ feet.
Conclusion: youth and age are alike.
Waiting at the well for the thief.
A thief has stolen a salted cheese. Since one always goes to the well after eating salted cheese, the thief will also come.
Waiting in the graveyard for the thief.
Waiting for the thief to return for the bolster.
After the cover is stolen, the numskulls conclude that the thief will certainly return for the bolster.
Waiting for the thieves to return for invoice of goods stolen.
Human milk as best diet (for baby).
Fool therefore will take nothing but milk from his wife and starves the baby.
Man is servant of the animals (for he supplies feed for them).
Men must have been calves once (for they are fond of milk).
Oil is cheap (or spilling oil is good luck).
Man hearing this breaks oil vessels.
Fool carries his wife to the remedy instead of the opposite.
Dipping into cold water to cure fever, since hot iron is so cooled.
Starving colt fierce from hunger, but fool refuses to feed it lest it become fiercer.
England must be full of widows.
So concludes widow’s daughter, who makes her living by spinning, when she sees so much warm goods from England.
False judgment of distance in clear atmosphere of mountain area.
Newcomer undresses to swim a five-foot stream.
He has walked all morning toward a mountain that seems only five miles away, but which is actually sixty miles from his starting point.
A man is robbed and later the same day is given much money.

A man who says that he is the servant of so and so is treated with great consideration. His companion, who says that he is a servant of God is put to work. He cannot understand why God’s servant should not be more important than the other.
Man honored above God: the dead hen.
A fool finds a dead hen and cooks it and serves it for dinner.
Fool waits for God to provide.
God blamed for scarcity of food.
Since he is an old man he should have known that more rain was unwelcome.
God blamed for letting pumpkin vines produce larger fruit than nut trees.
Poor man thinks idol in temple is poorer than he since it is naked.
Man says: “That’s the best horse in all England, but I have one in my stable worth ten of him.
A rustic refuses to believe reports about hell from a priest who has not been there.
The inconvenience of having a father: The numskull to his father: “If you had never been born I would get my grandfather’s estate.”
The fool lies still as the thief enters the house, hoping that the thief may find something so that he can take it back from the thief.
Robbed man blames thief for not warning him so that he could have witnesses to the theft.
Taking the seed out at night.
Numskull plants seed in daytime and takes it out at night. “Man must guard his treasures” (or “Growing in the daytime is enough”).
Three reasons for not giving alms.
Learn to swim before going into the water.
The queen has been told that the peasants have no bread.
King ignorant of famine says the people can live on pulse (sugar) and rice.
Loss of eating contest because of weak legs.
The sheep thinks that that is the reason for loss of the contest.
Why can’t we have holidays the year round?
Imitator of the pig’s cries applauded. Fool brings real pig but fails.

Thief brought to judgment for breaking into house blames mason for building poor house. Mason blames maker of mortar, who blames potter, who blames pretty woman who diverted his attention. She blames goldsmith who caused her to go for her earrings. Goldsmith has no one to blame but he is too old to make a good execution. Hence a shopkeeper across the way is convicted.
Innocent man executed because his neck fits the noose (or the like).
Men hang old bedridden weaver instead of young, valuable member of colony after the young man has accidentally killed an Indian.
The latrine is too small for the dining room table to go in.
The fool can sing in the small bathroom but cannot be heard from the minaret. He wants a bathroom built on the minaret so that his voice will carry.
A man believes himself wise because he has a book which he uses but does not understand.
As the fool starts for the doctor the wife changes her mind. He continues to the doctor so as to tell him about it and to say that now he need not come.
Useless trip to find a name the wife already knew.
Fool goes to astrologer for child’s name, but forgets it on way home. Later wife happens to use the word and reminds him.
Servant sent to doctor finds trip futile.

Doctor may not be in and, if he is there, he may not give the medicine. He may give the medicine but it may not have any effect; or, if it does have any, he has to die someday anyway and the medicine will not prevent him from dying.
A man who is away from home writes a letter to his wife but can find no messenger. He delivers the letter himself and then goes on back to where he has been.
Scribe cannot write a letter because he has bad leg.
Must carry letter in person since no one else can read it.
Fool writes letter very slowly: recipient cannot read fast.
Fool sleeps so as to avoid idleness.
Climb down as you climb up.
A peasant falls out of a tree. A neighbor advises him not to climb trees. Another suggests that he always climb down a tree with the same skill and rapidity that he climbed up.
Fool tastes every piece of fruit before giving it to his master.
Fools reprove each other for speaking at prayers.
Travelers say they will not have time to do so when attacked.
Boy cannot read a book written with smaller letters than those he was reading at school.
What becomes of the old moon?
Lightning made from the old moon.
Stars made from the old moon.
Numskulls try to throw the moon over a cliff.
Numskulls attempt to capture moon and bring it home in a sledge.
They get to the top of the hill a few minutes too late to reach it.
Chanticleer believes that his crowing makes the sun rise.
Disappointed when it rises without his aid.
Is today’s sun the same as yesterday’s?
Fools believe sun sleeps at certain woman’s house.
Bird thinks that the sky will fall if he does not support it.
Why everyone doesn’t live in the same place.
Same air at home as abroad.
Because the stars are the same.
Same climate at home and abroad.
Because his members look the same in the two places.
Falling star supposed to have been shot down by astronomer.
Dinner time comes soon in mountains because of rare atmosphere.
Clouds supposed to come from smoke.
A drunken man falls overboard but the skipper refuses to pick him up. “A man who is soaked in wine cannot drown.
A fool finding a nun in bed with a bishop and not seeing her face concludes that the bishop must have four feet and so announces it.
Peasants find a dead wolf and debate what killed it. A learned man shows that it froze internally from eating cold flesh.
Fool believing in omens refuses to prepare for death.
Bird has chirped five times, which he thinks guarantees him five more years to live.
Belief that island may be towed by ships to new location.
Husband takes back faithless wife on her oath to be faithful.
His wife has become a widow.
Numskull buys cloth used only by widows and is therefore convinced.
Gullible husband removes from wife’s garment dust gathered while she lies with another man.
Person made to believe that he is dead.
Wife makes her husband believe that he is dead.
Numskull is told that he is to die when his horse breaks wind three times.
When this happens he lies down for dead.
Man believes he is to die when he breaks wind.
Numskull is told that he will die when his mouth bleeds.
Man believes, he will die when water falls on his head.
Numskull believes he is dead when pumpkin falls on his head.
Man believes he will die when he gets a scarlet thread on his coat.
Fool, told yellowing soles of his feet sure sign he is going to die, digs his grave and lies in it.
The wife tells the husband that a certain pot of preserves is poison. He decides to kill himself and eats the preserves. He believes that he is poisoned and lies down for dead.
