Brain of snake said to be only cure for monkey’s disease.
Monkey to be killed by snake when he goes to hole.
Ogress wife demands eyes of six wives of raja or she will die.
Camel induced to offer himself as sacrifice.
Other animals feign to offer themselves to the lion as food. The lion eats the camel.
Man is being hauled up on the rope.
Rope of mountain-climber cut and victim dropped.
Barber killed when hero reports king’s ancestors need his services in heaven.
Man with deformed head slays his barbers.
Pretended exchange of confidences as to the one thing that can kill.
Hero tells enemies how he may be killed.
Secret of external soul learned by deception.
Daughter pulls out father’s magic life-containing hair.
As soon as it is taken out he dies.
Man carries written order for his own execution.
Man carries unwittingly an oral order for his own execution.
Leopard and crocodile both sent for the dog.
Neither has seen a dog nor have they seen each other. Man sends them to the same place saying that the dog will be there. They kill each other.
Fatal deception: changed message from oracle.
Dupe induced to stand under falling tree.
Tree cut down to get at victim in top.
Dupes lured onto tree-trunk bridge; fall to death.
Man is lured into sitting in a mechanical chair and is killed.
Magic horse lent by fairy in disguise brings about death of mortal.
Murder induced by bribery (lands, riches, wives).
Person thrown out of magic airship and killed.
Dupe persuaded to go to dangerous place; killed.
Brother causes brother’s death by sending him to robbers and giving false advice.
Under pretence of curing eyesight the trickster blinds the dupe.
Fool deceived into curing headache by removing his eyes.
Ashes as remedy for sore eyes.
The trickster pretends to make the dupe beautiful.
Making the beard golden: “such a one”.
A man named “Such a one” persuades an ogre to have his beard gilded. He covers it with tar and leaves the ogre caught to the tar-kettle.
The fox persuades the wolf to lie on the hay in order to be painted. He sets fire to it.
Making wife beautiful by burning her.
Burning children on promise of giving them fawn’s beautiful spots.
Trickster to give wings to tiger.
Trick: breaking legs for prowess in dancing (or for swiftness).
Pepper given as ointment for burns.
Biting on stone given as remedy for toothache.
Leopard wants teeth filed: large stone dropped from tree knocks all leopard’s teeth out.
Beetles and barley introduced into wounds on pretence of healing them.
Feeling pulse: doctor severs arteries instead.
Hare flatters other animals into letting it bite off their ears.
Deception into disastrous attempt to procure food.
The bear is persuaded to fish with his tail through a hole in the ice. When he is attacked and tries to escape, he loses his tail.
Dupe bound fast and then attacked.
Hair tied to basket so that dupe kills self when she throws basket down.
Basket tied to wolf’s tail and filled with stones.
Wolf is persuaded that it is filled with fish.
Bear persuaded to slide down rock.
Dupe persuaded to steal food: cannot escape.
Cannot escape through the entrance hole.
Jackal eating into elephant’s dead body becomes a prisoner when it dries up; is released when storm moistens hide.
The fox ties one end of the rope around the wolf’s neck, the other to the cow they intend to eat. The cow drags the wolf to the house where the man skins it.
Water-monster, trying to pull horse into water, is dragged to house where he begs for his life and is spared.
Bear throws hens to the fox, falls from the roof-beam, and is beaten.
Wolf brings cake from the window-sill.
He imitates the fox in so doing, but rings a bell, so that he is beaten.
Turtle induced to rob in a man’s garden.
Fox eats cake: gets brass pot caught on neck.
Thieving wolf persuaded to stick head through handle of jar of wine so as to be able to carry it off and also sing.
Dupe allowed to guard “king’s drum”: it is a wasp nest.
Dupe allowed to guard “king’s girdle”: it is a snake, which bites him.
Dupe persuaded to pick up biting ants.
Dupe persuaded to sit on ant hole.
Animal made to believe sound of swarming bees is that of her children singing in school.
Rushes to water to relieve stings and is drowned.
Dupe induced to strike at bee’s nest: badly bitten.
Animals are to eat one another up to avoid starvation. The fox persuades them to start with the smallest.
The fox persuades the wolf to do so.
The fox suggests eating his own brains.
The wolf, wanting to get brains, strikes his head against a tree.
Tiger persuaded to eat own eyes.
Dupe imitates trickster’s thefts and is caught.
Dupe made to sit on hot stone.
Jackal persuaded to come to fireplace for food.
Hot porridge in the ogre’s throat.
He is tricked into burning his throat.
Dupe persuaded to climb rope for food: rope breaks.
Stone (hard fruit) thrown into greedy dupe’s mouth.
Trickster pretends to give dupe magic power to produce food.
Dupe told he can get meat by putting hand up animal’s anus: animal drags him.
Jackal puts head in anus of sham-dead camel: caught and punished.
Dupe injures self on fence of thorns surrounding food-plants.
Dupe otherwise persuaded to voluntary self-injury.
Dupe lets himself be carried aloft by bird and dropped.
Flight by putting on bird feathers.
Water bird takes dupe to sea: shakes him off into water.
Elephant offers to let chameleon hold on to his tail: it is oiled and chameleon falls off.
Dupe induced to eat sharp (stinging, bitter) fruit.
Monkey “shares” ointment with tiger: produces sores.
Dupe persuaded to rub salt on wounds.
Dupe persuaded to scald self with hot water in order to learn languages.
The bear bites the seemingly dead horse’s tail.
Is dragged off by the horse.
Dupe persuaded that sheep have been lost in river.
Dupe induced to dive for alleged jewels.
Dragon attacks own image in mirror.
Robber persuaded to climb down moonbeam.
A man hearing a robber enter tells his wife aloud that he always makes a prayer and then enters the house by climbing down a moonbeam. The thief tries it and falls.
Dupe persuaded to get into grass in order to learn new dance.
Crocodile hides in strawstack and is burned to death.
Dupe allowed to guard “king’s litter”: sticks in mud.
The trickster gives the ogre the gun to smoke.
Deer persuaded to butt head into tree.
Serpent’s jewel is covered with spiked helmet so that when he tries to recover it he strikes and is spiked to death.
Dupe digs till he dies of exhaustion.
Rabbit entertains the wolf with his antics until the rabbit’s wife can change to another hole. The wolf continues to dig.
Dupe persuaded to transform self into animal.
Man dupes animals into turning their tongues upside down.
Duck persuades cock to cut off his crest and spurs.
Taught incriminating song or persuaded to wear incriminating clothes.
Trickster teaches a dupe a strange language.
The laborer teaches his master birds’ talk.
Puts him in a sack and beats him.
Cuts off tip of pupil’s tongue or orders him to lick cold iron
Peas strewn on stairs so that person will slip.
Fairy induces hero to dive into lake which makes person old.
Dupe tricked into sitting on hot iron.
Fox persuades bear to lie in the haycock and wait for sheep.
He sets fire to the hay.
Dupe tricked into breaking tabu by lying.
Dupe sleeps on the “king’s bed”: falls into well beneath and dies.
Persons duped into injuring each other.
Blind men duped into fighting: money to be divided.
Trickster says that he is giving one of them money to be divided with the others.
“I don’t believe you have a gold coin.”
Trickster handed money by each of four blind beggars, each thinking that member of group speaks.
Blind men duped into fighting: stolen meat.
The trickster steals one piece of meat. The blind accuse each other and fight.
Blind men duped into fighting: strings leading to water removed.
Ogres (large animals, sharp-elbowed women) duped into fighting each other.
Trickster strikes one so that he thinks the other has done it.
Enemies duped into fighting each other.
Missile thrown among enemies causes them to fight one another.
Object thrown into air causes enemies to fight over it.
Bird lighting on the heads of group of men causes them to kill one another with blows on the head.
Undesignated present starts quarrel for its possession.
Liar brings about fight between dupes.
Trickster tells lies to fishes and causes them to fight.
Jackal tells tales so as to get buffalo and tiger to kill each other; feeds on the meat.
Trickster attempts to bring friends to fight.
Calumniators try to bring friendly kings to fight, but fail at last.
Woman makes trouble between man and wife: the hair from his beard.
She tells the wife to increase her husband’s love by cutting a hair from his beard. Also tells the husband that his wife will try to cut his throat. He kills his wife.
Woman makes trouble between man and wife (to lick husband’s body).
Woman makes trouble between man and wife: to keep certain rendezvous.
Woman induces men to fight over her and kill each other.
Falsified message brings about a war.
Men disrobe and report they have been attacked: bring about war.
Message falsified to bring about death of lovers.
Dissension aroused in army by casting suspicion on general.
A general destroys everything except what belongs to the general of the enemy. Thus he brings about suspicion that the two leaders are in league.
Brothers duped into killing each other by slander that one of them is father to the other’s child.
Goddess arouses heroes’ jealousy and eternal fighting.
Treacherous counselor persuades king’s son to woo his father’s young bride whom he is sent to get, and as he tells the king that he is her lover both are killed.
God persuades hero to substitute a false bride for his father; this results in a fight where the son kills the father.
Dupe puts hand (paws) into cleft of tree (wedge, vise).
Dupe wishing to learn to play fiddle has finger caught in cleft of tree.
Dupe wishing to learn to play flute puts tongue in split bamboo.
Dupe caught in crack in ground.
Ogre helps tortoise who snaps jaws to and catches him.
Hero bends tree over but when he catches breath the tree shoots him to the sky.
Tree becomes light (after all honey has been collected from nests), springs back and kills tribe’s enemies.
A man is induced to get into a tree which magically shoots upward.
Dupe persuaded to climb tall tree.
The bear eats a horse which has a bell tied around its neck. The fox rings the bell and gets blamed.
The trickster takes an oath by touching iron (a trap). The dupe imitates but hits the iron so hard that he gets caught.
Animal gets bait from trap by luring another animal into it.
Dupe induced to sit on sharp stones (concealed as soft seat).
Ogre induced to sit on reversed harrow.
Wolf (lion) approaches too near to horse: kicked in face.
Wolf (lion) as sham doctor looks at horse’s foot: kicked in face.
Sow kicks wolf into stream when he comes close to baptize her pigs.
Thus she saves them from him.
Dupe tries to dig up alleged treasure buried in ant hill: bitten by snake and killed.

Peter and Christ are sleeping in the same bed. The drunken host returns home and beats Peter, who thereupon changes places with Christ. The host then comes in to beat the other lodger and beats Peter again.
Dupe persuaded to throw away his knife.
Later must go hungry because he has no knife to cut the meat.

A father sends his sons one after the other to pasture the goat. The goat always declares that he has had nothing to eat. The father angrily sends his sons from home and learns, when he himself tries to pasture the goat, that he has been deceived.
Casual words uttered by dupe used to cheat him of his property.

A miser is persuaded by his servant to fast nine days. He calls out on the fifth day “the half” and on the ninth “the whole”. She makes people believe that he is making his will and giving everything to her.
Animals hidden in various parts of a house attack owner with their characteristic powers and kill him when he enters.
Man persuaded to go to store with scythe.
Plot to induce king to commit a crime.
His line thus will forfeit succession.
Dupe tricked in race into falling into a pit.
Falling beam in cave kills travelers lured within.
Minister dupes raja into entering body of dead parrot, then enters rajah’s body.
Dupe deceived concerning the thunder; finally killed by it.
The dupe has asked the trickster to tell him when it thunders.
Sheep makes fox believe that the hunter is a priest, the dog his servant, etc.
Hot tin under the horse’s tail.
The smith promises to make the horse wild. The numskull on the horse’s back.
Rat leaves serpent behind, through spared to rescue him.

The two are imprisoned together in a sevenfold cloth covering. The serpent refrains from eating the rat so that the latter can gnaw the cloth for them. The rat gnaws his own way out and leaves the serpent.
Tiger persuaded to cross river carrying vat rim-upwards.
Trickster fills it with stones and tiger loses it.
A lover who is to be pulled up to his mistress’s window is left hanging in the basket in the public gaze.
Lover left standing in snow while his mistress is with another.
He later tricks her into standing a whole day in July in a tower naked exposed to the sun and flies.
Woman dares husband to try his sword on pile of clothing which hides her paramour.
Stops him just in time. Later the paramour entices her to come to him. Exposes her naked, except for face, to his friends.
Adulteress frightens paramour with cries of “Rape!” Then she removes her husband’s suspicion by feigning a fit.
Later the paramour tricks her to his room and shows her naked, except for face, to her husband.
Prostitute frightens lover with cries of “Thief!” Gets his money.
Is forced to dress as woman and discharge womanly duties including spinning.
Importunate lover induced to dress as woman and sift flour.
Importunate lover is induced to undergo series of humiliations.
Aristotle and Phyllis: philosopher as riding horse for woman.
The philosopher warns the king against uxoriousness. In revenge the queen beguiles the philosopher into letting her ride him on all-fours. The king comes and sees.
Hidden paramour taken to his own wife.
He hides in a chest. The chest is taken by a creditor who unwittingly delivers it to the paramour’s wife.
Lover caught on magic basin and left in embarrassing position.
(Lai l’épervier.) The chaste wife has them one at a time undress and hide. The husband and guests come and chase them off.
The entrapped suitors: the chaste wife tricks them into casks.
The husband takes the casks to the marketplace where he opens them.
The entrapped suitors: the chaste wife has them caught.
Forces them to work for her.
The entrapped suitor: tricked into room where he is left to himself.
Importunate lover imprisoned and starved: later given choice of lady or food.
Lover hidden by wife in room made to fall into deep pit of treacle.
Importunate lover (priest) is forced to hide in chest.
Husband takes the chest to the waiting congregation. Clever priest comes out enacting the resurrection of Lazarus.
Four importunate lovers are forced to hide in four-compartmented chest which is sold.
Importunate suitor enticed into sack and beaten by husband.
Priest caught in lasso by rival lover.
Mistress tells knight of priest’s demands. Knight has her give assignation, and arranges around her a string lasso which he pulls, and catches priest.
Importunate suitor has his head shaved and tarred and is put into a sack and returned to his men.
To get “nothing” and to show it.
Wife pushes lecherous king first into glue and then in the closet with feathers.
Suitors one by one enticed into graveyard and left together.
Suitors as corpse, angel, and devil.
First induced to lie in coffin, second to sit up with the “corpse”, and the third to carry a firebrand. “Corpse” thinks others are angel and devil. All come to blows.
First has him hide on thorns, second has him fall into a hole, third has him fall asleep in the street. In revenge he shows them naked, except for face, to his friends.
Girl asks importunate lover for weapon to use against her father.
Instead, she uses it to defend herself against the suitor.
Importunate lover beaten and sent on street bearing humiliating placard.
Importunate lover beaten with canes filled with straw.
He thinks he is severely wounded.
Obscene tricks are played on repugnant simpleton who wishes to marry.
Importunate lover is given a rendezvous.
Wife takes lover beneath tree where she has told husband to hide.
When he begins to kiss her, husband shouts “Keep a little for me.” Lover, shamefaced, runs away.
Woman tricks importunate lover with the head of a pike.
Thereafter he thinks the vagina is toothed.
Mistress deceives lover with a substitute.
Bride escapes from foolish husband and leaves goat as substitute in bed.
Mistress sends man’s own wife as substitute without his knowledge.
Chaste woman sends man’s own wife as substitute (without his knowledge).
Then the first woman’s husband is substituted for the importunate lover, who has his own wife seduced.
The woman has been asked for a rendezvous. She tells the suitor’s wife and they exchange places.
Chaste woman substitutes corpse for herself in the bed of an insistent suitor.
King’s daughter deceives king by substituting her maid.
Sometimes the trick is played by a rival lover.
Lover put off by deceptive respite.
Lover put off till girl bathes and dresses.
Suitors put off till web is woven.
Respite from wooer while he brings clothes all night.
The girl wastes time trying them on.
Girl refuses to dance with a devil until she is well dressed.
The devil brings things till the cock crows. Another girl asks for all the things at once and must dance until she dies.
Girl asks undesired lover to take off his boots.
She pulls off one partway and escapes.
Girl tells physician-seducer she cannot meet his wishes until after he bathes.
Prepares the bath herself and pours acid into it.
Woman leaves importunate lover waiting in her room.
Girl puts off consummation of marriage to undesirable suitor by saying her “stomach is sick”.
Girl asks undesired lover to follow her but not to step on her shadow.
Girl says she has made vow not to marry until pilgrimage is made.
Girl as umpire in suitor test (shooting arrows) escapes.
Importunate lover kept overlong at supper: must leave.
Escape from undesired lover by alleging menstrual period.
Abducted princess tells her abductor to wait for her menstrual period of 12 years to terminate.
Chaste woman refers lover to her husband for permission.
Chaste woman refers lover to his wife.
Lover deceived by false suicide agreement.
The woman persuades her lover to jump from a cliff; she will follow. She does not jump.
Lover’s anger softened by sham suicide attempt.
King tricked into sleeping with hag.
Disguise as man to escape importunate lover.
Girl plays at dice with her suitors: locks them up when they are defeated.
Usually by feigning sickness he induces the dupe to carry him and then boasts that the dupe always acts as his horse.
Feigns sickness and persuades dupe to carry him. Thus wins the girl.
Priest trapped in window and humiliated.
Trickster makes dupe believe that he is holding up a great rock and induces him to hold it for a while.
Fox pretends to be holding up the roof; hence cannot help the bear, who must do the threshing alone.
Fox pretends to be guarding the sky and watching the earth.
Dupe persuaded to guard hat supposed to cover something valuable. It covers a pile of dung.
Dupe persuaded to fight with alleged gold-dropping bear: trickster meantime steals his clothes.
The general hatches out an egg.
The page induces the general to take his place in sitting on the eggs. Then he calls the king to look.
Person hypnotized into believing himself transformed.
Man carried and dropped in mid-stream.
Threat to tell of amorous intrigue used as blackmail.
The bag of lies: threat to tell of queen’s adultery.
The boy, who is to tell the bag of lies, is stopped and his wishes granted.
Princess made to speak desired words when hero threatens to report (falsely) her amorous conduct.
Educated chickens tell of woman’s adultery.
A trickster undertakes to teach a woman’s chickens to talk. When he reports that they are saying that she has slept with the priest, she pays him off.
Man hidden in roof sees girl and lover and falls: they flee and leave him in possession.
Man having seen woman and lover from roof threatens to tell about it; is paid to stop.
Man hidden in roof (or elsewhere) sees girl and lover: blows horn.
They flee and leave him in possession.
Observer of intrigue insists on sharing in it (or enjoys the girl after putting the man to flight).
Lovers observed in intrigue make absurd excuses.
Amorous intrigue exposed and faithless husband humiliated.
Wife surprises husband in adultery and shames him into giving her all she desires.
Adulteress tells lover “I can see the whole world.”
Man abed with his wife is frightened away by an intruder who steals his clothes.
Abbess puts priest’s trousers on her head.
Suddenly called up while abed with the priest, she thinks to put on her coif. Discomfited by nuns whom she has denounced for incontinence.
Discovery of abbot’s (abbess’s) incontinence brings permission to monks (nuns) to do likewise.
Girl who cannot keep silent thereby provokes her rival to admit unchastity.
Girl refusing her lover final kiss provokes rival to admit selling kisses.
Woman draws a pelt to her instead of her husband.
A woman asks of her husband a hair which will magically draw him to her. He gives her a hair from a pelt.
Priest draws a sow to him instead of a woman.
He asks for a pubic hair which will draw the woman to him. Sow’s bristles substituted. Sow rushes to church.
Rascals pull off judge’s breeches and leave him exposed.
King induced to kiss horse’s rump: trickster then threatens to tell.
Opposing witnesses’s pockets filled with dung.
Hostile brother-in-law made king’s inferior by being tricked to hold his sword, while the king arranges his breeches belt.
Mortal woman seduced by a god.
Woman won and lost by a ruse.
Seduction by masking as woman’s husband.
Seduction by masking as woman’s husband: “Why—you have just left!” After the seduction the husband comes and the wife shows surprise.
Trickster kills husband and puts on his skin so as to seduce wife.
Husband’s twin brother mistaken by woman for her husband.
Seduction by wearing coat of invisibility.
Seduction by posing as a god.
Seduction by posing as Angel Gabriel.
Seduction on promise that issue will be the fifth Evangelist.
Seduction on feigned orders from angel to engender a pope.
Girl persuaded to sit on certain plant: seduced.
Man as sham doctor tells her how to heal her burnt groins.
Seduction by sham process of retrieving lost gem.
Seduction by sham process of repairing vagina.
Seduction by pretending to give childless man’s wife medicine.
When husband comes at cockcrow as he was told, trickster says he came too late and they must do it again.
Seduction attempted on promise of magic transformation: woman to mare.
Seduction by posing as a relative.
Seduction by posing as holy man (churchman).
Tricksters persuade women that they must share their marital intimacies with them.
Seduction attempted on threat of performing miracle.
Girl disguised as friar gets into priest’s bed.
Seduction by posing as teacher or instructor.
Seduction by pretending to instruct (or to need instruction) in marital duties.
Seduction under pretence of teaching a game.
Seduction upon false promise of marriage.
Seduction by offering protection against non-existing danger.
Lover’s place in bed usurped by another.
Master in serving-man’s place in woman’s bed.
Leper intercepts letter and takes paramour’s place with princess.
Old woman intercepts letter and takes girl’s place in man’s bed.
Vengeful paramours send syphilitic man to substitute in woman’s bed.
Man caught running by guards has to tell his destination.
One of the guards substitutes for him with his sweetheart.
Woman substitutes for her daughter in the dark.
Use of drugs to usurp lover’s place.
Woman drugs sister and substitutes for her with lover.
Moorish (black) girl substituted for mistress (in the dark).
Man intercepts love letter and takes lover’s place in elopement.
Devil comes to rendezvous instead of woman’s lover.
Trickster shifts married couples in bed.
Old man married to young woman and young man married to old woman. The shift is satisfactory to the young couple.
Seduction by man disguising as woman.
Man disguised as woman admitted to women’s quarters: seduction.
Man disguised as pregnant woman admitted to girl’s bed.
Seducer successfully disguised as washerwoman for fifteen years.
Man wishes to learn and gains entrance to learned girl’s presence in woman’s disguise.
Man disguised as woman abducts princess.
Man disguised as woman courted (married) by another man.
Man disguised as woman beguiles hostile chief.
Infatuates him and then kills him in drunken sleep.
Men disguised as women enter convent and seduce impious nuns.
Girl masked as man wins princess’s love.
The lovely ascetic (girl in man’s clothes) wins love of a rich woman.
Man disguised as gardener enters convent and seduces nuns.
Messenger from lover to girl-captive in harem poses as a singer who amuses the harem ladies in their apartments.
The girl comes to the man’s wake or funeral.
Hero feigns death and is copulated with by divine maidens.
The guest in the conjugal bed feigns sleep as he effects seduction.
Seduction by asking for sham cure for sham illness.
Cautious farmer seeks laborer who knows nothing about sex. Trickster makes silly explanation of copulation of animals. When admitted into service, seduces both farmer’s wife and daughter.
Disguise as animal to seduce woman.
Girl tricked into man’s room (or power).
The princess must answer all questions by “No”. By clever framing of his question the hero wins her to his desires.
Seduction by taking aboard ship to inspect wares.
Girl seized when she tries to take jewels.
Seduction by enticing woman to inspect wares in tent.
Seduction by having maiden placed in floating chest.
Seduction (or wooing) on an aerial journey.
Seduction (or wooing) by stealing clothes of bathing girl (swan maiden).
Magic helper brings girl to hero’s bed.
Girl tricked into man’s room (power)— miscellaneous.
Fresh hides spread on grass; girl slips up and is deflowered.
Woman enticed to upper world on a stretching tree.
Seduction by luring woman to platform to look for distant ship.
Woman enticed into man’s room by feigned illness.
Trickster dupes two girls into submitting to test.
Girl tricked by use of drugs.
Subsequent pregnancy used to force her into marrying seducer.
Seduction by priest who insists on woman having confession in his own house.
Trickster agrees to carry old woman and girl across stream: carries girl across and rides off with her leaving old woman on other side.
Leak in roof over woman’s bed: in rain must go to bed with trickster.
Entrance into girl’s (man’s) room (bed) by trick.
Entrance to woman’s room in hollow artificial animal.
Entrance to woman’s room in golden ram.
Princess’s curiosity aroused and the golden ram carried into the room. The youth is concealed inside.
Entrance into woman’s (man’s) room by hiding in chest.
Man carried into woman’s room hidden in basket.
Entrance into woman’s room in lamp stand.
Heroine in hiding-box which is bought by prince.
Man in magic hiding box bought by girl’s father.
Man drawn up into female apartments on rope.
Man drawn up into female apartments in basket.
Man disguised as woman carried into princess’s room: marries her.
Tunnel entrance to guarded maiden’s chamber.

Two youths pass the night with a family where all sleep in a common room, with a cradle at the foot of one of the beds. The moving of the cradle in the night confuses those walking about so that the strangers sleep with the wife and the daughter.
Enters her tower by means of artificial wings (or on flying horse).
Hero flies on magic carpet to maiden’s room.
Man is ushered into maiden’s room by maidservant.
He then takes the latter’s place in the mistress’s bed.
Lover gets into maiden’s room by means of a ladder.
Other means of entering into girl’s (man’s) room (bed).
Lover disguised as porter gains access to princess’s room.
Disguise as madman to enter girl’s room.
Trickster gains access to woman’s room disguised as peddler.
Man disguised as groom enters mistress’s room.
Man feigns sick in order to enter room of princess skilled in healing, and woos her for his friend.
Trickster gains access to woman’s room by pretending he has news of her absent lover.
Access gained by the aid of rival’s mule.
Man tries in vain to learn the identity of his friend’s mistress. Mounts his friend’s mule, which takes him to the secret rendezvous.
Lover visits guarded maiden while harper puts mother to sleep.
Access for seduction gained by removing locks.
Lover gets self carried into beloved’s house to wait for clean clothes after a purposeful fall in mud.
Man burns down own neighboring house to gain access to bedroom of beloved.
Entrance into woman’s room through concealed door.
Trickster pretends to seek lost ball by woman’s bed: seduces her.
Admission to woman’s room by means of cap of invisibility.

A procuress throws pepper into the eyes of a bitch so that she weeps. She pretends to the virtuous woman that the bitch is a woman transformed because of failure to respond to her lover. The woman is persuaded.
She shows remorse when she hears of lover’s death.
Ruler promises to release her brother (husband) but afterward refuses to do so.
Trickster offers food for woman’s favors which will completely satisfy him.
He refuses payment on grounds that he is not satisfied.
Seduction by bearing false order from husband or father.
The youth is sent to the house to get two articles. He meets the two daughters and calls back to the master. “Both?” “Yes, I said both!” replies the master. The youth has his will of both daughters.
Trickster masking as girl’s father advises intercourse with trickster.
Seduction by bringing false order from husband.
Trickster asks husband for one thing and the wife for another.
Trickster friar seduces woman under pretence of administering forgotten sacrament.
Fox sleeps with tiger’s wife by giving her deceptive message from her mate.
Seduction by bearing false order from mother.
He follows her mother’s order according to his own interpretation.
Trickster masking as bridegroom tells bride that he comes at her mother’s request.
Seduction by bearing false order from lover.
Altered letter of execution gives princess to hero.
On his way robbers steal the letter and change it so that instead of being killed he is married to the princess.
The husband appears before payment can be made to wife.
Girl shows herself naked in return for youth’s dancing hogs.
Beggar buys right to sleep before the girl’s door, at foot of bed, in the bed.
Transformed person sleeps before girl’s door, at foot of bed, in the bed.
Is disenchanted upon admission to the bed.
Progressive purchase of favors: the anatomical progression.
Seduction by begging into woman’s room to get warm.
Innocent girl sells her “love” and later receives it back.
When she tells her mother what has happened, she is beaten. Thinking to right matters, she demands that the knight return what he has taken.
Seduction of person ignorant of sexual intercourse.
Obscene trick used to seduce woman.
Friar adds missing nose (fingers) to unborn child: foetus is imperfect and he will substitute for absent husband.
Is praised by the latter on his return.
Woman abducted by giving her medicine which appears to have killed her.
Second daughter won by representing first as dead.
Monk persuades a father to set daughter afloat in box: monk seduces her.
Seduction by making woman jealous of co-wife.
Lover steals bride from wedding with unwelcome suitor.
Parson deceived into marrying his intended bride to her real lover.
The parson thinks it is a mock-wedding, but it turns out to be real.
Lover’s foster brother (friend) steals bride from wedding with unwelcome suitor.
Father tricked into giving away disguised daughter in marriage.
Rat changes name and wins wife intended for leopard.
Man gets bridegroom drunk and enjoys the bride.
While chief is performing suitor task, rival steals the bride.
Woman engaged to marry by trick.
Princess tricked into engaging herself to suitor rejected by her father.
Fool passed off as very eligible young man by matchmaker.
Seduction by alleged vision promising woman to man.
Seduction of wife by alleging that husband’s vision compels him to leave home.
Trickster pretends lameness and is taken on woman’s back: violates her.
Trickster throws corpse into river and accuses princess of murder: marriage to avoid scandal.
Female overpowered when caught in tree cleft (hole in hedge).
Man won over by woman’s obscene trick.
Lecherous trickster seduces women from tree and loses them.
Trickster sends letter ordering bearer detained and meanwhile steals bearer’s wife.
Husband persuaded to dig up a treasure buried in an ant hill.
He is poisoned by a snake and his wife taken.
Trickster by magic has intercourse with woman across stream.
Trickster and girls play obscene tricks on one another.
Woman seduces boy by feigning illness (chill, etc.)
Man coveting his friend’s wife causes her to leave her husband.
Friend mutually agree to beat wives. Trickster only pretends to do so while other beats his and angers her.
Woman tricked into standing naked in stream; medicine put into water.
Guest at inn is told that there is but one available bed: that of the mistress.
Sextus says he will kill her and leave a naked slave in her bed to bring dishonor on her house.
The father wants his daughter’s child to be a bishop.
The taming of the wild prince.
Lost in the woods the little prince grows up among wild animals; lets no one come near him. Only a servant girl succeeds in taming him.
Assuming unusual names, the servant deceives the girl, her mother, and her father.
Seduction: trickster shows girl how to store up warmth for winter.
Woman secures man’s spear (arrow), lures him with it into her hut.
Teacher seduces pupil left in his charge.
Plowing the field: horse and harness destroyed.
The youth is told to come home from plowing when the dog does. He beats the dog so that it runs home; then he destroys the horse and harness and goes home.
Lighting the road (or painting the house red).
It is lifted off and carried away.
Take care of the stopper! The son puts the stopper into his pocket, and all the tar (beer) runs out.
Rascal has been told to cut wood.
Closing the door tight: with iron nails.
Whetting the knife: the whole blade whetted away.
Threshing grain: granary roof used as threshing flail.
Mowing grass: the meadow torn up.
Cleaning out manure: piles it high.
Covering the whole wagon with tar.
Told to fill locked pen trickster chops up wagon and mules and throws them in.
Sowing grain: does so in unplowed field.
Trickster saws legs of table so that it collapses.
Fixing fences: trickster cuts fence down.
Ordered to build a bridge not of wood, stone, iron, or earth, the trickster uses the carcasses of cattle.
Ordered to cast eyes on this or that, the trickster kills animals and casts their eyes at the object.
Washing him in boiling water or currying him with a razor.
Horse twists intestines out of himself.
Told to bring in sheep laughing and dancing, trickster cuts off their upper lips and breaks their legs.
To drive cattle to jungle: trickster kills a bull every day.
Tying the cattle: trickster ties them so tightly they are strangled.
Watching the goats: “Hit them if they wander.”
Trickster exchanges master’s tame horse for vicious bullock.
Caring for the child: child killed.
Child taken to defecate over ant hole.
To heat water for master’s bath.
Servant pours boiling water on him.
To cover house with straw: suffocates mother under straw.
Trickster deceives dupe into killing his own children.
Threatens to jump from tower with lord’s children unless lord blinds himself. Lord does so but slave jumps with children nevertheless.
Master’s mother killed: wood heaved on her head.
Cuckold feigns to be asleep when paramour calls.
Wife of philanderer gets revenge by having an affair herself.
An adulteress returns home late at night and her husband refuses to admit her. She threatens to throw herself into the well. The husband goes after her. She enters the house and bars him out.
Adulteress refuses to admit husband under pretence that he is a stranger.

(Lai of the Tresses.) A woman leaves her husband’s bed and has another woman take her place. The husband addresses her, gets no answer and cuts off her nose (hair). In the morning the wife still has her nose (hair). The husband is made to believe that it has grown back by a miracle (or that he was dreaming).

A chaste wife substitutes a maidservant for seducer. A finger and ring are cut off as proof of wife’s unfaithfulness (chastity wager with husband). Refuted by husband, who knows they are not his wife’s.

A husband insists that his wife take oath that she has been intimate with no one but himself. The paramour masks as ass-driver. She hires an ass from him, falls down, and lets him pick her up. She then swears that no one has touched her except her husband and the ass-driver.
Adulteress gets rid of husband while she entertains lover.
The husband in the chicken house.
The husband returns unexpectedly and surprises his wife with her lover. She makes the husband believe he is pursued and hides him in the chicken house.
Husband duped into doing penance while rascal enjoys the wife.
Husband duped into believing he is in purgatory.
Mistaken for lover whom he has told them to beat.
Husband, dressed in wife’s clothing, is beaten by forewarned paramour. The latter says that he is testing the wife’s fidelity to her husband.
Husband hides in curtain to catch paramour.
On entering, paramour threatens to kill husband if he should appear.
Husband hides in chest to catch paramour.
Adulteress locks up hidden husband and meets lovers.
Wife has hiding husband carried off in basket by thieves.
Wife throws husband down precipice so she can be with lover.
Adulteress has lover unload wood on doorstep.
Adulteress sets husband to watch for intruder while she entertains the paramour.
Illness feigned to call physician paramour.
Adulteress pretends to go to say her prayers.
Adulteress gives paramour tryst in house of ill-fame.
Meets husband who leaves in shame.
Husband chases mare while the wife entertains the paramour.
Adulteress throws small coffer out of window.
While the husband retrieves it the paramour changes hiding places.
Lover masks as pregnant woman: adulteress sent by husband to act as midwife, meets lover.
Adulteress together with lover while husband sleeps.
Wife drugs husband and visits paramour.
Adulteress makes excuse to go and attend to bodily needs: meets lover.

The husband has locked the surprised paramour in a chest while he fetches his family as witness of his wife’s unfaithfulness. She frees the lover, substitutes an animal, and discountenances the husband.
Physician treating man’s eye covers his one good eye.
Girl covers nurse’s one good eye so that she cannot see her lover.
Adulteress extinguishes light to hide her paramour.
Adulteress covers husband’s eyes during incantation.
Adulteress persuades husband to milk cow with his eyes blindfolded: meets lover.
The faithless wife asks her gullible husband how he would act if he were blind.
The husband closes his eyes; meanwhile the lover escapes.
Wife washes husband’s hair hiding his eyes while lover escapes unseen.
Wife has husband look for hole in pot she has bought, allowing lover to escape unseen.
Wife shows husband her milk-filled breasts and squirts milk in his eyes allowing lover to escape unseen.
The lovers as pursuer and fugitive.
The wife is visited by two gallants. When the husband approaches, one goes out with drawn sword; the other hides in the house. She convinces her husband that she has given refuge to a fugitive.
One lover disguised and carried out of house by other.
The wife has the lover put on a robe and stand in the corner; she tells the husband that a tradesman has left the robe and will return for it. The other lover comes and she gives him the “robe”.
Paramour in vat: disguise as vat-buyer.
Husband thinks he is testing the vat.
Lover hidden in chest with feathers.
Husband believes he is a devil.
Husband thinks he is a demon.
When surprised with the wife he tells the husband that he has been trying to force the woman, with no success. The wife supports the statement.
Paramour disguised as cloth merchant is surprised by the husband.
He asks the woman to be paid for a pretended sale.
Paramour leaving love-tryst is met by husband.
Paramour escapes by pretending to be returning borrowed basket.
Escaping paramour said to be a deity.
The wife makes the husband, who has seen the adultery from the tree, believe that the tree is magic or that he has seen double.
Husband who has surprised wife and paramour is made to believe that he has had an illusion.
Paramour placed in chest and covered with clothing.
When husband comes in she drops candle and sends him out for another, allowing lover to escape unseen.
Lover escapes behind the sheet which wife holds up to show her husband.
Husband busied with performing task while paramour escapes.
Husband in hanging tub to escape coming flood.
The priest who has thus duped the husband enjoys the wife.
(Inclusa.) Woman goes from one to the other. Her husband is made to believe that the woman next door is her sister.
Adulteress falls in mud at lover’s door.
She deceives her husband by saying that she must enter and clean her dress.
The Lord above; the lord below.

A husband returning home surprises a woman and her paramour and a numskull who has blundered in. The woman hides the numskull in the bed and the paramour under it. The husband, who is leaving on a journey, lifts his hands to heaven and says, “I commend you to the Lord above.”
Friar’s trousers on adulteress’s bed: relic to cure sickness.
The husband is duped into believing that the friar has come to visit the sick.
The husband returns unexpectedly to find his wife entertaining the paramour with a sumptuous feast. He is made to believe the feast is in honor of some newly-weds.
She suspects the fraud and persuades him that she knew the ruse and was testing him. He begs forgiveness.
Husband transformed to goat must witness wife’s adultery.
Adulteress tells her lover how she loves her husband.
She thus deceives the spying husband under the bed.
Adulteress tells how she may save her husband’s life.
Discovering him under the bed, she tells lover that at temple she has learned that her husband is to die soon unless she prevents death by sleeping with a strange man. The husband is satisfied.

(Tristan and Isolt.) Husband goes to wife’s love tryst and hides behind a tree. The wife, having learned of his presence, tells lover that he should not allow their innocent relations to lead to gossip.
Adulteress transforms her husband into an animal to get rid of him.
Adulteress transforms man to stone up to the waist.
Woman has husband made monk while he is drunk, so as to get rid of him.
Wife feigns death and slips out to lover.
Death feigned so man can live with mistress.
Sexton’s own wife brings her offering.

The priest grants to the sexton the offerings brought by all women whom the priest has loved. The priest always calls out “Take” when these women offer. The sexton’s own wife comes. The priest calls out “Take!” (Cf.
Husband frightened by wife’s paramour in hog pen.
The husband sees the paramour who has hidden in the pen and says, “Who are you?” “I am a miserable hog.” The husband thinks that his hogs are possessed.
The marked coat in the wife’s room.

A procuress obtains a woman for her client by leaving a marked coat in her room. The husband drives the wife away and she joins her lover. The procuress then goes to the husband and alleges that she lost a coat with certain marks. The husband is deceived and takes the wife back.
Husband unwittingly instrumental in wife’s adultery.
Not knowing lover’s identity, husband takes him to his wife and entrusts him to her care. He then leaves on a trip.
Wives wager as to who can best fool her husband.
Woman warns lover of husband by parody incantation.
Woman warns lover of husband by singing song.
Adulteress makes believe that her suspicious husband is insane.
Woman has paramour steal her husband’s clothes.
Paramour gains entrance disguised as the husband. The husband without his clothes is driven away from his home.
Wife surprised in adultery feigns death.
Comes “back to life” on hearing husband say he has seen nothing.
Lover carried away on mistress’s shoulders so that his footprints will not be visible in the snow.
Lover leaves horse outside house as husband comes up: wife tells husband their cow has foaled a horse.
Unfaithful wife communicates with lover by pouring milk into stream.
Wife’s attendants on trip chase wrong man as suspected lover and miss real lover.
Husband deceived as to noise made by hidden paramour.
Adulteress detected: husband secretly drops dye on her dress.
Adulteress detected by food she prepares for paramour.
Adulteress detected by food she prepares for paramour.
Husband returns home secretly and spies on adulteress and lovers.
Husband returns secretly and kills unwelcome suitor.
Husband feigns blindness and avenges himself on his wife and her paramour.
Husband feigns illness to surprise wife with paramour.
The husband sets house afire and ousts hidden paramour.
Trickster sets fire to barrel of tow in which paramour is hidden.
The paramour, naked, runs out carrying wisps of burning tow. The trickster tells the husband that he has raised the devil.
Husband carries off box containing hidden paramour.
Dying woman lures paramour into chest.
Asks husband to bury chest with her.
Chest containing paramour unwittingly taken away by husband.
Lover hidden in hen-coop discovered by husband.
The naked lover hides himself in a sooty barrel. The husband receives from a curious gentleman a good sum of money for showing him the “devil”.
Hidden cuckold reveals his presence by rhymes. He responds to the rhymes made by the wife and paramour concerning their entertainment.
Adulteress binds husband’s eyes and causes him to sing incantations concerning the adultery.
Husband discovers wife’s adultery by riddling conversation.
In this indirect manner the wife confesses and promises reform.
Husband discovers paramour’s love letter in his wife’s purse after having made her drunk.
The husband prepares to castrate the crucifix.
The artist’s wife’s paramour poses as a crucifix when caught. When he sees the husband’s preparations, he flees naked.
The husband meets the paramour in the wife’s place.
Husband hides in wife’s room and kills paramour.
The wife sends her maid to investigate. The maid falls in and finally the wife herself.
Husband (god) traps wife and paramour with magic armor.
Husband proves intrigue by secretly blacking paramour’s mouth.
When he returns, his wife’s face is black.
Blades (broken glass) to wound and detect wife’s lover.
Cuckolded man shuts wife’s paramour in chest and lies on the chest with latter’s wife.
Cuckold unwittingly lies with wife on chest containing her hidden paramour.
Husband tricks wife into riding a mule which has been denied water.
On fording a stream the mule plunges into the water.
Husband in disguise begs food of his wife’s suitors.
Husband outwits wife and paramour—miscellaneous motifs.
Rebukes them for not shutting the door.
Illness feigned to go to mistress.
Husband leaves bed to go to serving maid.
Husband catches paramour by using wife’s pre-arranged signal.
Husband persuades wife to light wicks and carry knife in hand before committing adultery: lovers frightened away.
Husband pretends that his wife’s privates tell him of her adultery.
Husband discomfits paramour and wife by clever remark showing that he knows all.
Wife persuades him he has killed thief.
Trickster discovers adultery: food goes to husband instead of paramour.
Trickster discovers adultery: gets food prepared for paramour.
Trickster as sham magician makes adulteress produce hidden food for her husband.
Trickster makes woman believe that her husband is coming to punish her adultery.
Trickster sends his master running after the paramour.
Though the master does not know of the adultery, the lover is thoroughly frightened.
Trickster as sham magician buys chest containing hidden paramour.
Sham magician has paramour fall in a trap.
Has trained bird to cling to him.
Trickster discovers woman’s paramour and hides him in outhouse: rewarded by husband.
Second lover burns paramour at window with hot iron.
God Vishnu in shape of nephew scares and torments his aunt’s lover.
Lover’s gift regained: the broken (removed) article.
The lover breaks (or removes) an article of household equipment and convinces the husband that for that reason the wife has confiscated that which he gave her as a present.
Lover’s gift regained: horse and wagon as gift.
The lover regains gift of horse and wagon by pretending to the husband that the wife has confiscated them because he brought wood of uneven quality.
Lover’s gift regained: borrowing from the husband and returning to the wife.
The lover borrows money from the husband with which to corrupt the wife, later telling the husband that the money was returned to the wife during the husband’s absence.
Lover’s gift regained: accidental discovery of identity.

The lover, ignorant of the identity of the husband, tells him of his experience with the wife. The husband persuades the lover to lead him to the scene, where the wife is compelled to restore all but a small part of the money.
Lover’s gift regained: piece of cloth as gift.
The lover regains by a ruse and thievery the borrowed piece of cloth which he has presented to his mistress.
Lover claims payment for cloth in the presence of the husband.
The woman returns the cloth but puts a live coal in it. Destroys his whole supply.
Lover demands return of cloth on threat to await the husband’s return.
Lover’s gift regained: jewelry as gift.
The lover presents the wife with a valuable piece of jewelry, which he regains by pretending to the husband that he has left it as a pledge.
Lover’s gift regained: anser venalis (goose as gift).
The lover regains his gift by a ruse (obscene).
Lover delays the gift of the goose hoping to obtain greater favors.
Lover’s gift regained: refusal to leave bed.
Lover’s gift regained: spending money to purchase lover’s worthless goods.
Lover’s gift regained: payment with worthless money.
Lover bargains with the husband. Pays him with worthless money.
Husband gets gift which paramour has given to wife.
After seducing priest’s wife, peasant demands earrings as price of silence.
He thus avenges himself on priest who has cheated peasant’s wife of her earrings.
Husband duped by paramour into taking his wife to him.
Innocent confessor duped into being go-between for adulteress and lover.
By following suggestions in her false accusations to confessor the lover reaches her side.
Wife takes servant’s place and discovers husband’s adultery.

The husband says that he is going into a state of meditation with a cloth over his face. He substitutes a servant and goes to his mistress. The wife finds the deceit and takes the servant’s place. On his return the husband tells the supposed servant of his adultery.
Paramour feigns loss of genitals in order to obtain the husband’s confidence.
Adulteress uses the public baths as a meeting-place with her lover.
A naive remark by her child exposes the deception to the husband.
Woman excites peasant (secretary), who draws line on floor and dares her to cross it.
When she does, adultery is committed.
Seventy tales of a parrot prevent a wife’s adultery.
The parrot keeps her interested until her husband’s return.
Faithless wife kills magic parrot which has betrayed her.
Peacock left as spy on adulterous wife.
Dog guards chastity of master’s wife during his absence.
Paramour sends prostitutes in disguise to take mistress to “convent”.
Husband is deceived by the ruse.
Adulteress disguised as boy elopes with paramour.
Student extends his course so as to enjoy the professor’s wife.
Complacent in all except kissing. Explains that her mouth is the only part of her body which has promised fidelity to her husband.
Faithful wife in disguise saves husband from punishment for adultery.
Deceiver falls into his own trap (literally).
Arranges a trap or pitfall but is himself caught.
Pitfall arranged but victim escapes it.
Man falls into sacrificial grave prepared for others.

Rich man orders poor people to dig a grave in order to bury all in it as sacrifice to avert famine. But a Christian frees them and promises those who become Christian a living. The rich man himself falls in the grave and dies.
Thief-catcher caught by his own magic club.
Deceiver falls into his own trap—miscellaneous incidents.
Substituted caps cause ogre to kill his own children.
The hero and heroine change places in bed with the ogre’s children and put on them their caps so that the ogre is deceived.
Substituted string causes ogre to be killed.
Intended victim of cannibal is marked by thread around ankle. Changed in night to host.
Guest to be killed suspects plot and forces host to sleep in his bed.
Brothers come home and kill their father.
Girl takes place of impostor in marriage bed; impostor’s mother beats her, thinking she is heroine.
Noose changed so that ogre’s daughter is dragged to death.
Kid puts one of tigress’s cubs in his place: she eats the cub.
Message of death fatal to sender.

(Gang nach dem Eisenhammer.) A man is sent by the king to burners of a kiln who have been instructed to throw the first arrival into the fire. The intended victim goes elsewhere and the king’s son (or the man’s accuser), who next arrives, is burned instead.
Person sends wrong man to sleep with king’s daughter.
In revenge villain orders whoever first enters temple to be killed. Villain accidentally enters and is slain.
Poisoner poisoned with his own poison.
Would-be poisoner forced to drink poisoned cup.
Person trying to blow poison on another is himself poisoned.
Wife poisons husband who in turn poisons her.
Before he dies he forces her to drink from the same cup.
Person gives his wife a poisoned drink; she pours the two drinks together.
Poisoner’s own son takes the beverage intended for step-brother.
Son who intends to poison father drinks the poison by mistake.
Snake killed by incantation he has taught clever woman.
Father delivering daughter to be eaten by cannibal is himself eaten.
The ogre plans to burn the hero’s moccasins while they are camping together, but the hero exchanges the moccasins.
Marooned man reaches home and outwits marooner.
The father-in-law has the youth hunt eggs on an island and deserts him, but the youth outwits him.
Marooned man hides himself in ogre’s clothes and outwits him.
Hero given arrows with soft points and sent after dangerous enemies. The deception discovered and the enemy discomfited.
Old woman planning to kill hero in swinging game by cutting rope is killed when hero cuts the rope first.
Tiger in sheep’s clothing stolen by sheep-thief.
Thief climbing rope discovered and rope cut.
He has tricked the guardian of the food-supply in the tree (by imitation of the owner’s voice or the discovered pass-word) to let down the rope.
Lawyer agrees to pay debt on winning his first case.
He refuses to plead so as not to pay. Debtor sues him for double the amount due him. If he wins he has to pay and if he loses he has to pay double. He settles debt.
Woman who engages false bridegroom for her daughter has plans go astray.
Monkey instead of girl in floating basket: hermit made laughing-stock.
He has persuaded girl’s foolish father to place her in the basket. Prince takes girl and leaves monkey in her place.
Earl killed in combat with man he has undertaken to kill.
Treacherous counselor killed in treacherous ballgame he himself has arranged.
Boiling water meant for cooking hero used for man who has prepared it.
Sons have servant impersonate dead father and falsify his will.
Servant deceives them by favoring himself.
The bribed boy sings the wrong song.

The sexton steals the priest’s cow. The next day the sexton’s son sings, “My father stole the priest’s cow.” The priest pays the boy to sing the song in church. But the sexton teaches the boy a new song, “The priest has lain with my mother,” and this is sung in church.
Fox leads ass to lion’s den but is himself eaten.
When he gets there the ass kicks him so that he falls on the lion’s bed.
Cock’s advice proves disastrous to himself.
He causes the ox and the ass to rebel but the master learns the cause of the trouble and kills him.
Partnership of Honesty and Fraud: Fraud loses.

Fraud has cheated his partner, Honesty. They hire a housekeeper. Fraud is to have use of her right side, Honesty of her left. The left side is of little use. Fraud falls in love with her and pays Honesty double all his losses to relinquish his rights.
They have killed the cock for waking them too early, but their mistress punishes them.
Flattering foreman tricked by his master.
Ambushed trickster killed by intended victim.
Husband intending to push wife down mountain is pushed over by her.
Mole as trickster killed in his own tunnel.
He tricks the fox by going through the tunnel and eating the common food, but the fox sees the molehill and kills him.
Animal strangled by victim which he tries to eat.
Woman ordered to strip has lover turn his back; pushes him into water (pit).
Woman bitten by own fierce watchdog.
Woman who tries to push husband into river falls in when he steps aside.
She drowns because she has tied his hands and he is unable to aid her. (She also thinks he is blind because she has fed him rich food to induce blindness.) (Cf.
(Pathelin.) On the advice of a lawyer, the client feigns insanity when arraigned in court. When the fee is demanded, he still feigns insanity.
Lawyer’s client therefore refuses payment of fee.

The trickster meets a man in a narrow place in the road and calls out to him to make room. The man refuses and the trickster turns over the cart. In court the trickster plays dumb. The plaintiff says, “He is not dumb; he called out to me several times to get out of the way.” Damages are assessed against the plaintiff for negligence.
Unjust official outwitted by peasant who quarrels with him and thus turns the attention of the ruler to the abuses.
The order for six loads of snow.
The order is given by the king in winter. The courtier waits until summer to present the order. Gets money as substitute.
A lover is let down into a girl’s room at night in a basket. The spying parent stumbles into the basket and is jolted about by the lover’s confederate.
Trickster sells dog for mutton or for opossum. He later eats the dog which has been given to a friend of his by the purchaser.
Unjust banker deceived into delivering deposits by making him expect even larger.
In order to make the impression of honesty he delivers the one chest of money. The ten chests which he then receives are filled with stones.
Blind man gets back his stolen treasure by making thief expect a larger one.
Buried money is stolen. Blind owner pretends that he is going to bury more. Thief returns the money hoping to get all. Blind man recovers original treasure.
Blind man asks thief to invest a larger sum for him.
The greedy thief puts back the stolen money hoping to get more. The blind man recovers his money.
Dwarf himself falls in love with girl he has seduced by magic love, and loses her as he is forced to remove his magic.
Sage’s advice followed: he is killed so that sacrifice can be mixed with his blood.
Bear (tiger) substituted for woman in floating box; kills villain who tries to steal the woman.
Swindlers allowed to hide money: proves to be basket of stones.
Pretended sick man aroused by beating.
Woman, who pretends to faint, comes to life when beaten by magician in order to drive out alleged evil spirit.
Magician challenged to make good his false claim.
Says he can take black and white dogs and make them gray and then reverse process. Trickster furnishes gray dog and challenges magician to show his power.
After the culture hero has instituted death, his own child dies and he repents in vain.
Inventor of death machine is first to use it.
Disguised trickster beaten by man he is trying to frighten.

Man decides to frighten another (or his son or servant). He dresses in a sheet; his pet monkey puts on a sheet and follows him. The person who is doing the scaring hears the victim say, “Run Big Fraid, run; Little Fraid’ll get you.” The scarer sees the monkey in the sheet, runs home.
Tables turned on procuress by chaste wife.
The old woman is enticed into the wife’s room, beaten, and driven forth naked.
Seller of pardons robbed by man whom he has pardoned beforehand.
The defence declared good by the judge.
The treasure-finders who murder one another.
Two (three) men find a treasure. One of them secretly puts poison in the other’s wine, but the other kills him, drinks the wine and dies.
Tail sticking from ground betrays killing of calf.
So arranged by servant in revenge on his master.
Men exchange jobs because each is made to believe that the other’s is easier.
The woman as cuckoo on the tree shot down.
The anger bargain is to cease when the cuckoo crows. The ogre’s wife climbs the tree and imitates the cuckoo. She is shot down.
A man in place of a cuckoo.
Disliking early rising, the servant kills devil’s mother or grandmother, who crows in place of the cock.
Teacher instructs pupil in the art of love: cuckolded.
Student, ignoring woman’s identity, seduces the teacher’s wife, and reports success to him. The teacher makes futile attempts to surprise wife with pupil.
Tries to avoid paying tax by hiding eggs in his breeches. The collectors make him sit down.
Trickster makes believe he has found a purse (which he had filled with lead).
Merchant claims it and pays ten crowns for it. Trickster wins ensuing suit.
Ogre made to believe small hero is large: overawed.
Tiger made to believe porcupine bristle is his enemy’s hair: overawed.
Weak animal (man) makes large one (ogre) believe that he has eaten many of the large one’s companions.
Weak animal shows strong his own reflection and frightens him.
Tells him that this animal is threatening to kill him.
Weak animal shows strong his own reflection and makes him believe that it is the head of the last animal slain by the weak.
Man shows ghost its own reflection and frightens it.
Man shows demon reflection and frightens him.
Bluff: only one tiger; you promised ten.
Child (or shepherd) calls out to the small hero (ape, hare) and makes the tiger (ogre) think that he is lucky to escape alive.
The wolf flees from the wolf-head.
The sheep have found a sack and a wolf-head. They make the wolf believe that they have killed a wolf, and he flees in terror.
Enemies frightened away by making them think they will be eaten.
Spirits frightened away by making them think they will be eaten.
Leopard frightened away by report of lizard’s presence.
Trickster pretends to hunt certain tree with which his ancestors have killed tigers.
Bluff: small (lame) hero makes demon believe he is a god and threatens to eat him.
Bluff: hero to brother, “You take one and I can manage the rest.”
Trickster purports to be deity’s messenger to procure demon-skins for his drum.
Demons bribe him instead of devouring him.
Ass claims to have killed cow: frightens tiger.
Lion frightened away by stabbing at it from inside iron cage.
Large animal frightened by smaller showing him well rope (for his tail), curds (for spit), winnowing fans (for ears).
Tiger made to believe that his captor has eaten many crabs.
Tiger fears crabs and releases him.
Fox overawes lion cubs by his boasting and eats their food.
Hare as ambassador of the moon.
Hare claiming to be ambassador of moon shows elephant the moon irritated in a spring. Elephant is persuaded that the moon is angry.
Big shoes in front of the barn.
Man makes giant shoes and places them so that ogre thinks a giant lives there.
Ogre overawed by hero’s boasts about marvelous relatives.
Bluff: thunder said to be the rolling of hero’s brother’s wagon.
Bluff: millstones said to be pearls of hero’s mother.
Bluff: huge cauldron of tar said to be kitchen-pot of hero’s mother.
Bluff: harrow said to be comb of hero’s mother.
Bluff: plow said to be hoe of hero’s mother.
Hero proves himself a cannibal by trick vomit-exchange.
Hero frightens dog into giving up eating men by pretending to eat own entrails.
Monkey pretends that his house always answers him.
Goat pretends to be chewing rock.
“Dogs are chasing you,” says ox to jackal.
Really water gurgling in the ox’s stomach.
Tiger thinks sound of water dropping is sound of dreadful monster: flees.
Giantess frightened of leaving cave because of hero’s statue in entrance.
Tiger frightened at hearing unknown wind.
The bear trainer and his bear.
(Schrätel und Wasserbär.) Ogre is driven out by hero’s bear. The next year the ogre asks, “Is the big cat still living?” Hero says that it now has many kittens.
Wages: as much as he can carry.
To get rid of the boy the troll offers him as large wages as he is able to carry. Boy says that this will be too much, that he will be contented merely with what the troll can carry.
Ogre made to believe hero has withstood fire.
Hero escapes and after the room he has been in is burned he returns and is found sitting in the ashes. “It was a bit hot,” he says.
Giant persuaded that hero has pushed hole in wall with bare hand.
Dog pretends to be calling dog in the moon when he barks.
He is invited but told that guests will include the Virgin Mary, Thor the Thunderer, etc. He stays away but sends the finest present.
Bluff: hero professes to be able to perform much larger task than that assigned.
Told to bring in a tree, the hero asks, “Why not the whole forest?” The ogre is frightened.
Bluff: told to bring home a tree, hero prepares to bring home six.
Told to shoot one or two wild boars, hero asks, “Why not a thousand at one shot?” The ogre is frightened.
Bluff: told to bring home an ox, hero prepares to bring home ten.
Told to get water, hero demands bucket large enough to bring in the whole well. The ogre is frightened.
Bluff: told to bring water in an ox skin, hero prepares to dig a canal.
Wrestler claims to be able even to carry away a mountain.
Hero threatens to pull the lake together with a rope.
Hero threatens to haul away the warehouse with a rope.
Trickster threatens to throw weight into a cloud: ogre intimidated.
He has formerly been caught in a vise. On his approach, the man’s wife stands on her head and ogre thinks her legs are a vise.
Bear frightened away by man threatening to cleave its skull with his penis.
He meets a woman who, upon being told what man had threatened, shows him a vestige of the cleaving she once got. Only partly healed.
Ogre terrified by an iron man.
In order to save the king’s daughter from the ogre an iron man is forged.
Bluff: provisions for the swimming match.
In a swimming match from a ship the hero takes a knapsack of provisions on his back. His rival is afraid and gives up.
In a contest in climbing the mast the hero falls into the rigging. “You do the same thing,” he challenges. The sailors are persuaded of his expertness.
Bluff in court: the stone in the purse.
A poor man has a stone in his purse to throw at the judge if he is sentenced. The judge thinks that he has money to use as a bribe and acquits him.
Trickster’s boasting scares his powerful opponent from contest.
False boasting of having killed his foster-brother makes his men follow the boaster.
Goat singing a threatening song bought off with food and jewels.
Sham threat: “In earnest or in jest?” A man asks another who has brushed against him: “Did you do that in earnest or in jest?”—“In earnest.”
Sham threat: something he has never done before.
Two who had challenged each other agree to hold a sham duel.
Sham threat: if I were not a philosopher I should break your head for you.
Girl’s sham threat in order to evade husband till lover returns.
Sham threat of war holds ships back so that there suddenly are enough men to man defending ship.
Sham dream prophesying shipwreck makes people leave ship so that there is room enough for man who wants to go.
King menaced into giving his daughter by means of borrowed fleet.
King persuades men to follow him, pretending that he is going to make peace with his brothers, instead battle.
Bluff: insult repeated as harmless remark.
The trickster makes an insulting remark, but when called on to repeat what he said he changes it so as to turn aside wrath.
Boast where the master cannot hear.
The servant boasts that he has scolded his master.
When he is looked at too threateningly hero feigns failing ability to go on horseback.
Threat to build a church in hell.
When the man makes this threat, he is let out of hell.
Bluff: wealth gained by seeming to be in the king’s confidence.
Courtier asks the king for a reward that will cost nothing. He gets permission to listen to the king’s devotions. He now receives bribes because of his apparent influence.
Shoemaker offers to trim the peasant’s feet to fit the shoes.
The peasant prefers to accept the ill-fitting shoes.
Herdsman threatens invasion with enormous herds: bought off.
He hires himself as herdsman of all his master’s flocks for ten years. He then sends notice to surrounding peoples that he is coming with his master’s flocks to graze. They bribe him to stay away.
Trickster falsely reports impending invasion from his own people.
Receives money to buy them off.
Adventurer on otherworld island sees great hornless oxen guarded by giant: tries to frighten them.

“Why dost thou frighten the stilly calves?” says the huge herdsman. “Where are the dams of these calves?” asks the adventurer. “They are on the other side of yonder mountain,” said he. So he went thence.
Miracle must wait till one man is sacrificed.
No one volunteers and it does not need to be performed.
Host serves many rare vintages and gets a reputation for his wine cellar. But there is only a small jug of each vintage.
Man falsely claims to have killed elephant with his flat hand.
Fox threatens to catch bird, who feeds him her young as appeasement.
He threatens to push down tree or to fly.
Sham duel in order to bring about recognition.
Feigned ignorance about person’s identity in order to tell one’s frank opinion of him.
Feigned ignorance of person’s identity in order not to reveal king.
Feigned ignorance about the whereabouts of hero’s weapons and horse in order to keep him as monk.
Illiterate man pretends to be weeping because he cannot make others understand the book he is reading.
Woman frightens robber away by telling him parrot’s cry is husband’s voice.
Disguise by putting on clothes (carrying accoutrements) of certain person.
Lover disguised in slain enemy’s clothes.
Taking king’s place by changing dresses.
Dog procures disguise from magician to frighten tiger.
Lover disguised as other knight in order to reach sweetheart.
Goddess in disguise visits earth and is waylaid by thieves.
They set her free after she promises to tell them the fate of the new-born prince.
Deity disguised as old man (woman) visits mortals.
God disguised as doctor cures mortal.
Deity takes form of particular person to visit mortals.
Fate takes form of Brahmin’s pupil in order to lure him to his prophesied death.
Angel takes form of certain person.
Deity takes form of animal to visit mortals.
King disguised beaten by his own men.
Incognito king helped by humble man.
Incognito king is asked by humble man to aid him.
Incognito king joins robbers: to take only six shillings.
The robber tells him that he must take no more, since the king has so many robbers.
He is beaten for showing courtesy. Realizes his folly and returns home.
Prince disguises as another prince to woo princess.
Incognito king is given hospitality by fisherman.
Ruler disguises as goblin to frighten uxorious priest.
King disguises as common soldier and is killed.
Queen flees husband’s persecution disguised as knight.
Disguised queen visits her husband and begets child with him as assigned.
Incognito king rewards farmer for gift.
King disguised as peasant flees battle.
Incognito king comes to the aid of an enemy who has refused to vilify him.
Incognito king rewards strangers who treat him as companion.
Lecherous prince disguises as merchant in order to kill his grand-children.
King in disguise of merchant is given hospitality by enemy.
King in disguise to spy out his kingdom.
Fallen king in disguise recognized by former ally and helped.
King in disguise as one of his own men rescued in fighting alone against four.
Disguised husband wins his faithless wife’s love.
Disguised husband shows his wife that he is not repulsive, as she thinks him.
Disguised husband shows his wife that he is not a good-for-nothing as she thinks him.
Disguised husband spies on his faithless wife.
Woman in disguise wooed by her faithless husband.
Prince disguised as merchant seduces a queen.
Wife substitutes for princess, who has been jailed with husband.
Wife disguised as fakir makes her husband, the king, fulfill her will.
Husband twits wife regarding “bought kiss”; she makes him buy one from her by disguising herself.
Disguise with hood dropping low over the face.
Pious pilgrim dies unknown in his father’s house.
Girl in menial disguise at lover’s court.
Hero in menial disguise at heroine’s wedding.
Scholar disguised as a rustic along road answers questions of school inspector in Greek, Latin, and Hebrew.
Nobleman disguises as cobbler to woo woodcutter’s daughter.
Queen disguised as peddler sells children poisoned cheese.
To avoid having his gold hair seen, the hero covers his head with a cloth and says that he has the scaldhead.
Lover approaches mistress disguised as fool.
Sharp man pretends to be stupid so as to be included in plans and conversation of plotters.
Disguise as deformed men to secure entertainment.
Youths have been advised never to serve a man with a red beard. The trickster dyes his beard black.
Veiled adulteress flees with paramour who has enlisted duped husband’s aid.
Youths wear false beards (of grass, wool).
Disguise as hairy man by putting on lambskins.
Disguise by cutting one eye out.
Beautiful woman blackens face as disguise.
Bad breath and forked tongue reveal identity of snake-king in guise of human.
Lover masks as doctor to reach sweetheart.
Girl disguised as doctor exposes queen’s paramour who is masquerading as woman.
Poor girl masks as doctor and is made court physician.
Trickster masks as doctor and punishes his cheaters.
Girl masks as doctor to find departed lover.
Disguise as physician to poison enemies.
Woman masks as lawyer (judge) and frees her husband.
Twelve men in disguise as carpenters are engaged to build hall for the king’s wedding: they abduct the bride.
Lover disguised as monk or friar meets sweetheart.
Lover masks as anchorite to reach sweetheart.
Man beats wife for spending too much time at church. Wife has maids dress as her patron saints and when the husband repeats the beating she calls on them for help. The husband is beaten.
Woman disguised as angel of death.
Shipwrecked men call themselves by false names.
Service in disguise in order to seduce king’s daughter by putting love charm in her food.
Lover in disguise as duke’s son takes service under king with his followers in order to abduct his sister.
Multiple disguise: one person disguising successively seems to be many.
Disguise of man in woman’s dress.
Husband disguises as woman to spy on wife.
Boy disguises as woman to embarrass incontinent priest.
Disguised man takes bride’s place: deserts, leaving a she-goat in his place for the foolish bridegroom.
Disguise as a weeping woman to attract attention.
Disguise of woman in man’s clothes.
Boasting coward exposed by wife who masks as highwayman and robs him.
Woman disguised as pilgrim engages lover in conversation and learns of his faithlessness.
Girl in man’s clothes avenges her father.
Wife disguises as a man and outwits landlord of inn when he tries same trick he has played on her husband to get all of his goods, etc.
Disguise of woman as a soldier.
Virgin living disguised as a man and unrecognized in a monastery becomes abbot (St. Eugenia).
Woman in male disguise made king.
Woman in male disguise made minister.
Priest disguises as devil and “haunts” neighbor’s house.
He thinks it is the work of demons. He sells them his house cheaply.
Wolf puts flour on his paw to disguise himself.
Girl marries lover who thought her dead.
On reviving she changes her name and disguises her appearance. Eventually marries her former lover.
Monkey dresses in dead mistress’s gown; frightens household.
Friar disguises as soldier and steals from concubine.
Warriors whitewash weapons thus disguising identity of one of their number who bears white-handled battle-axe.
Disguise as older brother to obtain blessing.
Husband and wife disguised as brother and sister.
Disguise as dupe’s daughter after having killed her.
The Virgin Mary substitutes for a mortal.
The nun who saw the world (Sister Beatrice).
The Virgin takes the place of the nun in the nunnery while the latter is living a life of shame.
A knight hears masses so long that he absents himself from a tournament. The Virgin takes his place.
Virgin Mary substitutes for woman whom husband has pledged to the devil.
Living person acts as image of saint.
Man acts as statue of saint in order to enter convent.
Wife deceives husband with substituted bedmate.
Bride has maid sleep in husband’s bed to conceal pregnancy.
Wife sends mistress to her husband disguised as herself.
Wife takes mistress’s place in husband’s bed.
Wife takes mistress’s place in husband’s bed: husband sends message of death.
Wife takes mistress’s place in bed but is deceived in turn.
Husband had tired of the mistress and had previously substituted servant.
Wife takes mistress’s place in husband’s bed.
The husband, unaware of the substitution, asks his friends to share his good fortune.
Wife substitutes for her sodomist husband.
Wife substitutes an old woman for herself in her husband’s bed.
Wife has maidservant impersonate her while she goes to her lover.
Husband deceives wife with substituted bedmate.
Husband has his strong servant substitute in bed with strong wife.
The supernaturally strong wife is about to kill her husband.
Husband has servant substitute in bed.
Instructed not to deceive him while he is calling on mistress.
Substitute bridegroom to save husband from poison maiden.
Groom deceives bride with substituted bedmate and hides self in order to learn the secret she has promised to tell.
Fairy visits queen in her husband’s shape and begets son with her.
Warrior deceived into attacking substituted pillar-stone.
King, fearing death at hands of enemy, forces follower to take his place on throne.
Deception by substitution: wife substitutes calf for beggar whom drunken husband wants to catch and abuse.
Substitution of children to gain inheritance.
Deceptive report of birth of heir.
Queen tells king anxious for an heir that she is to give birth to a son, but that ill will befall the son if king looks upon him.
Impotent husband deceives wife by having a substitute in virility test.
Ruler has favorite perform tasks so that he may himself win a bride.
