Slaughter of children to prevent fulfillment of parricide prophecy.
Child mutilated to avoid fulfillment of prophecy.
Wooers slain to avoid fulfillment of prophecy.
God swallows his pregnant wife to prevent birth of son whom he fears.
Exposure of pregnant woman to avoid fulfillment of prophecy concerning future child.
Murder of pregnant woman to avoid fulfillment of prophecy.
Children swallowed one after the other as they are born for fear one of them will overcome father.
Delivery of child fated to rule retarded in order to avoid fulfillment of prophecy.
Sword that is to kill one is weighted and sunk so as to avoid the prophecy.
Stone that is to kill one powdered and thrown into distant sea.
Man whose death has been prophesied takes refuge in church, but is accidentally slain through window by arrow directed at stag.
Man told by Death he will die where he stands sells everything and moves to another town. He goes for a ride on a mare which runs away with him and throws him on the spot he so dreads, killing him.
Prophecy of misfortune for prince avoided successfully in one respect.
Queen dies from fright from evil prophecy.
Child pronounces blessing according to which countries are to be filled with what they are later famous for.
Prophecy: son of certain name will become king; all sons given the name.
Prophecy: meeting will take place only after death.
Prophecy: hunters will encounter certain wild boar.
No one to go security for a satirist.
Unintentional curse or blessing takes effect.
The person in despair curses himself to sink with palace into the earth.
Man pursued by hatred of the gods.
Saints curse by ringing bells against offender.
Hermit curses men who kill his pet bear and all the men die.
Curses on places because of offensive answer to saint.
Saint curses books hidden by inhospitable host: no man shall read them.
Giantess lays a curse on the one on earth who eventually hears her.
Curse by girl in revenge of the murdering of her foster father.
Priest curses sinner: even his grave shall not rest.
The grave rolls like a wave.
Curse by head of religious order.
Curse by other wronged man or woman.
Curse given at birth of child.
Will fall with full effect on objects at which it is aimed.
Curse: god to live life of a cat for twelve full years in house of huntsman on earth.
Curse given to negate good wish.
Odin gives man life three times the normal; Thor ordains that in each he is to commit crime. Odin gives him the choicest weapons; Thor denies him landed property, etc.
Given with the gift of twelve men’s strength.
Curse: eternal life without eternal youth.
Curse by “building a fire of stones” in fireplace.
The person who removes the stones is cursed.
Release from curse with birth of child.
Curse transferred to another person or thing.
Curse changed by God into blessing.
Curse on everybody on earth who listens to the fatal mentioning of trolls’ names, is evaded by person in cave, because he is in the earth.
Curse mitigated by deity when superhuman task is performed.
Release from curse by burning vomit.
Release from curse by putting pins around horse’s heart and then boiling it.
Release from curse by burning animal in straw pile.
Release from curse by heating the colter of the plow in the stove.
Release from curse by pricking louse and hanging it on wall.
Release from curse by putting a five cent piece in the churn.
Release from curse by putting a piece of silver in the gun.
Curse: fire to burn hands and feet.
Curse: hand of person cursed to drop off.
Wicked stepmother cursed to have fire lit under her.
Curse of sterility on wife of enemy.
Curse: head to split in seven pieces.
Curse: to be plagued by nightmares.
Curse: to be carried off by evil spirit.
Curse: to be swallowed by a siren.
Curse: not to taste food from own table.
Curse: prince to fall in love with witch’s daughter.
Curse: “What I carry may you carry; what you carry may I carry.”
Cat thus causes ungrateful pregnant woman to bear cats and herself to bear twin girls.
Jealous sisters curse the child one of them may have by the god Thor, so that it never will grow nor thrive.
Curse: man (poet) to kiss a leper.
Curse: hero not to be able to stand the sight of blood.
Girl bewitched so that no man will remain faithful to her.
Curse: hero to remain as dead till the curser dies.
Dying father condemns weak son to be servant of his brothers.
Curse: man’s sword will fail in danger.
Curse: when brothers’ swords bite the very best, they will all be killed by a single man.
Curse: she-wolf to carry off man’s genitals.
Curse: lack of food, shelter, good company.
Curse laid on unborn child; it is stillborn.
Giant cursed: may neither heaven nor earth receive him.
Curse: undertaking dangerous revenge of father.
Curse: to sink into the earth.
Curse: corpse to be put in three different places after person’s death.
Hero cursed to restlessness (except on boat or in tent), till he sees girl.
Curse: not to be able to love the same woman more than twelve months.
Thrall cursed to sit on chest and yell and never have rest.
Curse: couple to wander until new seat of race is pointed out.
Curse: woman will not travel far.
Curse: descendants of nine robbers never to exceed nine.
Curse on village: descendants never to exceed certain number.
Curse of a woman against her caste: they should remain unclothed and untaught.
Curse: cow will give red milk.
Curse: milk will not turn to butter.
Curse on a city: never to grow.
Curse on river or sea: no fish in it from that day.
Curse on lake: fire from lake will burn the forest around it.
Presence of cursed person brings disaster to land.
Whomsoever demons curse is blessed, and vice versa.
Gambling caused by possession of men by evil demons.
Bankrupt gambler gets supernatural power and wins back his fortune.
The miracle of broken die at gambling saves man.
Dice made from bones from graveyard.
Stakes not claimed by winner, who insists on another game.
Own body as stake: to be taken as slave.
Right of succession to the throne lost in gambling.
Supernatural adversary in gambling (witch or giant).
Devil makes wager with builder of Cologne Cathedral.
Playing game of chance (or skill) with uncanny being.
The parson plays cards all Saturday night, goes to sleep at church, and calls out the names of the cards.
Luck in gambling from compact with devil.
A man’s wife is deceived in order that he may lose in gambling.
Trained rat upsets pieces in gambling game: trained (or transformed) cat chases it away.
Wagers on wives, husbands, or servants.
Though the man has foolishly bargained everything away, she praises him and he wins the wager.
Wager on the most obedient wife.
The husband tames his shrewish wife so that he wins the wager.
Wager: raja’s daughter will bring servant dinner in field.
Merchant ignorant that she is his wife.
Husbands wager that they will be able to do what wives tell them to do.
A man makes a wager on his wife’s chastity. In spite of unsuccessful attempts to seduce her and of false proofs presented, he wins the wager.
Wager on sex of unborn child.
Fathers whose unborn children are affianced wager as to mastery in the house.
The servant is sent to a neighbor’s where he is made drunk and is seduced by the neighbor’s wife. He tells the master all.
Wager: who can call three tree names first.
The bear names different varieties of the same tree, so that the fox wins the wager.
Wager about tree names: learned and common names.
Brahmin gives learned names but servant’s common names are confirmed by illiterate peasants.
Wager: it is an auspicious day.
In spite of all misfortunes wagerer insists that he is right.
Loser of shooting wager to go naked into thorns for bird.
Wager: woman to turn somersault in middle of public square.
It is performed not exactly in the center of the square; hence she loses.
Wager that falsehood is better than truth.
Left to unjust umpire, so that falsehood wins.
Wager: more doctors than men of other professions.
The trickster feigns toothache. Everyone suggests remedies. He takes down their names as doctors and wins the wager.
Wager: fortune made from capital or from working at vocation.
Wager: woman can be forced to give alms.
Trickster announces that only those who have deceived their husbands are exempt.
Wager: to begin sermon with illustration from card-playing.
First object has proved to be ordinary. King induced to make large wager that second is ordinary.
Wager: whose hunger is it more difficult to appease—that of man or that of beast? When nuts are strewn before master’s well-fed guests, they snatch and eat them.
Wager: to swallow egg with one gulp.
Tricksters give numskull egg with chick in it. Fool hears chick peep as he starts to swallow his egg, but he says that the chick peeped too late.
Purchase of box without knowledge of its contents.
Wager to win or lose according to whether jackal howls or ass brays before game is finished.
Father hides wealth to keep son from gambling it away.
Inexorable fate: no day without sorrow.
A king, who has made decree against sorrow on a certain day is blinded by a swallow in his sleep.
Inexorable fate: death from violating tabus.
Man cannot die: snake will not bite him though it is provoked by him.
Man fated to become king becomes so despite fact he breaks his tooth in which his luck resides.
Fortune comes to deserving and undeserving.
Luck (fate) thought of as a goddess.
Home of Fortuna in other world.
Home of Fortuna on island (in otherworld).
Fortune has one eye, watches over everybody.
Fortune’s wheel turned by dead king in mountain.
Fortune with pair of scales in his hands weighs man’s balance.
Man thanks earth for saving his life; had he fallen into well he would have blamed Fortune.
Giant is clerk to God of Destiny and measures out mortals’ spans of existence.
Bad luck put into a sack.
Good fortune resides in an object.
Casket with Good Luck in it given to men by Zeus.
Personification of Good Luck lives in man’s forehead.
Man’s luck resides in his tooth.
Personification of Good Luck leaves palace since king is destined to die that night.
Luck can be found in certain place.
Ship’s course left to the winds that it might be carried where fate wills it.
Dog tries to catch its fate in its own tail.
Buffalo’s fate in bamboo growing from head.
Ill-omened face of king; harbinger of evil. India: Thompson-Balys.
Child born with objects that indicate fate.
Spirit of new-born child in uniform.
God has determined fates of everyone.
New-born child with a weapon and a game animal: fated to be hunter.
Mother shown what would have been the evil fates of her children if they had not died.
Newborn girl fated to be a courtesan.
Seventh daughter predestined to be magician.
At parting of three roads are equivocal inscriptions telling what will happen if each is chosen. Brothers each choose a different road.
He upon whom feather (wisp) falls to be king’s fool.
Luck determined by whether a crooked-necked demigod is looking at one.
King to be victorious as long as he rides muzzled gelding.
Districts named from first person met in each.
Lots cast to determine luck or fate.
Lots cast to determine who shall undertake adventure.
Lots cast to determine father of illegitimate child.
Different kinds of luck attending persons born on the several days of the week.
Days of the week on which certain tragic deaths occurred.
National disasters occur always at the same date.
Monday and Wednesday as unlucky days.
Turning right-handwise in certain place brings luck.
Judas Iscariot spills salt at the Last Supper.
Luck changing after change of name.
Luck changing after change of place.
Unlucky to have man in house while cloth is being dyed.
Wife brings bad luck to the husband’s family.
Spirit of adversity brings bad luck to house.
Passenger brings bad luck to ship.
The king is to become lucky when he puts on the shirt of a lucky man. The only man who says that he is lucky has no shirt.
Feast for those who have not known sorrow.
Dying Alexander’s letter to his mother orders such a feast.
The wealthy merchant becomes a beggar, due to the judge’s boots he acquired through exchange (theft).
Nature of luck and fate—miscellaneous motifs.
Luck or intelligence? Dispute as to which is the more powerful.
Man with intelligence remains poor (is brought into court). Saved by mere luck.
Which is more important, learning or wit?
Which is more powerful, wealth or wisdom?
Which is more beautiful, nymph of Luck or of Ill-Luck (Luck when coming, Ill-Luck when going).
Weaver married by Wealth to a princess to show Wisdom that he is the more powerful.
Destiny better than work, show, or speculation.
A peasant makes a little by his work; a nobleman more by his outward show; a merchant still more by speculation; but a prince most of all by his destiny.
Luck only with money that is earned honestly.
Cast-out princess prospers because of Good Luck.
Man not fated to die cannot be killed.
Unprotected son makes fortune; protected son has bad luck.
Prodigal son favored over faithful son.
Disagreeable and disliked youth as favorite of Fortune.
Careful builder outside when storm comes is killed; careless builder saved.
Refused hospitality, he must sleep outdoors. The house burns down.
Loss of eye saves man from execution.
Man to be buried with king. Gets off because he lacks an eye.
Broken leg saves man from fatal fight.
King has ordered that he be killed in a fight. He breaks his leg and cannot take part. Meantime the king learns of his innocence.
Man chosen for execution because he is fat.
King’s counselor expelled from a court thereby escapes accompanying the king, who is killed by robbers.
Only crippled cow not driven away by robbers.
Fortunes of the rich man and of the poor man.
The Fortune of the rich brother tells the poor brother to seek his luck under a bush. The poor man goes there and Fortune tells him to become a merchant. He becomes rich.
Snake turns to gold in answer to dream.
Woman tells dream of pot of gold. Robbers overhear but finding only snake in pot turn it loose on woman’s bed. It turns to gold.
Money lost twice: recovered third time.
Fugitive woman burdened with child saved; childless woman killed.
Man who derided another’s faith in the stars becomes respected astrologer.
Hero fails to meet the man he seeks, though they are close to one another.
Girls make wish that they may marry king (prince, etc.).
Wish realized that all women should fall in love with man at sight.
Lost object returns to its owner.
Lost articles found in interior of fish through virtue of saint.
Brooch lost by saint found in fish.
Unavailing attempt to get rid of slippers; they always return.
Angel helps to find lost pin.
Money cannot be kept from where it is destined to go.
Miser told that his hoard is to go to poor man. He hides it in a trunk and throws it into the sea but it drifts to the house of the poor man who tries in vain to restore it to its owner.
Husband’s magic gift returns to him.
Wife gives husband’s magic gift (fruit) to lover, who presents it to a dancing girl, who sells it back to the husband.
Child borne off by tiger, which is caught by griffin, which is killed by lioness, which rears child with her whelps.
Man granted power of winning at cards.
First objects picked up bring fortune.
Man must have drinking horn; stumble reveals one as he departs on search.
Man finds treasure he refused as gift.
Man robbed and penniless entertained by wealthy widow and enriched.
Wrecked man saved on coffer of jewels; becomes rich.
Man who is impoverished is given high post by princess in disguise.
Leopard tied in bag in water floats to shore and finds a mate.
Grateful to trickster who has tied him up.

The husband leaves his wife, who has given birth to fourteen girls, thinking he is persecuted by bad luck because of failure to have a son. On the seashore, the girls find precious stones. The wife, now prosperous, finds her husband among beggars.
Boast of poor boy made good by fate: he boasts to elder brothers he will build a palace on a certain spot; accidentally comes on treasure trove and makes good his boast.
Bad luck follows man who shoots stork.
Wishing to escape it, the luckless couple build themselves a new home.
Persecution by a god so that will of deity can be followed.
The poor man in some way banishes his bad luck and becomes prosperous. Out of envy his rich brother sets it free; it then follows him.
(Placidas, Eustacius.) His goods are destroyed, his wife carried off by a ship captain and his children by animals.
Man captured by pirates is maimed, crippled, blinded.
He is patient through it all. Finally he is elected ruler by his dead master’s subjects.
Man who aspires to greater wealth loses all.
When he is about to be rewarded by king the latter dies.
Man who loses fortune marries widow of his rich master.
A luckless man becomes successful in all his undertakings when he marries a lucky woman and lives by her luck.
The luckless son and his envious father.
Seeing a luck-bringing animal at his son’s house, the wizard father orders it to be destroyed, but the grandchildren eat of its meat and become fortunate.
Messengers announce successive misfortunes to warrior as he sets out for war.
Tells of death of father, mother, brother, and sister, but he refuses to turn back.
After many misfortunes the man is apparently safe. The wall falls on him.
Escape from one misfortune into worse.
Stag escapes from hunters to be eaten by lion.
Finally the farmer beats him living and will not spare his hide when he is dead.
Halcyon builds nest on sea-cliff to escape land hazards.
Fugitive slave takes refuge in mill house, where he must work harder than ever.
Daw fleeing from captivity caught in trees by thread around foot.
Old man burns self with gunpowder, and then burns himself worse when he pours hot water over his body.
Train of troubles from lost horseshoe nail.
Master tries to go on in spite of the loss.
Train of troubles from sparrow’s vengeance.
A man runs over the dog, friend of the sparrow. Through the sparrow’s vengeance the man loses his horse, his property, and finally his life.
Train of troubles for seven brothers for having destroyed bird’s nest.
Whether man begs all day or for an hour he gets only a small basket of grain.
Person brings bad luck to others.
Girl brings ill luck and death to everyone she comes in contact with.
The sun brings all to light.
The murderer repeats as he sees the rays of the sun, the last words of the dying man, thus betraying the crime.
Murder revealed by unusual names of boys.
The dying man leaves message to name his sons “O God” and “O king” (or the like). This arouses the king’s curiosity and brings the murder to light.
Murdered man calls on cranes, the only witnesses of the murder, to avenge him. The cranes follow the murderer and point him out.
Ravens pursue murderer who has killed two children.
Murder discovered through knowledge of bird languages.
Murderer through miracle suspected of theft; murder thus discovered.
Murder discovered on digging foundations of house.
Ship will sink if murderer is aboard.
Murder will out: murderers quarrel under influence of drink and reveal crime.
Criminal confesses because he thinks himself accused.
Criminal confesses because of misunderstood animal cries.
Criminal confesses because of misunderstanding of a dialect.
Wife misunderstands husband’s remark and confesses.
Thief imagines that group of people in street are talking and laughing at him; he confesses.
Criminal in church mistakes words of service as accusation.
Sheep thief confesses when preacher says, “All we like sheep have gone astray.”
Oxen bear dead usurer to gallows to be buried.
They are allowed to go where they will.
Separation of persons caused by looking for water.
Separation of twins through being carried off by beast.
Child follows bird and loses its mother.
Persons fall asleep on rock, which magically shoots upward.
Separation by being on different banks of stream.
Man, thinking it an enemy, flees as sweetheart comes after him in pursuit.
Princess accidentally elopes with wrong man.
Man unwittingly causes death of daughter.
Son returning home after long absence unwittingly killed by parents.
Eavesdropping man in disguise as devil killed unwittingly by daughter’s lover.
Eavesdropping wife hidden in bushes killed unwittingly by husband.
Unwitting murder because of insane illusion.
Man kills son thinking that he is cutting a branch.
Women, driven mad, devour their infants’ flesh.
Mother kills son thinking him a wild beast.
Things accidentally fall and kill person.
Dagger in wall above bed falls and kills girl.
Has been placed there by her lover.
Knife accidentally strikes girl’s throat and kills her.
Prince’s arrow accidentally grazes breast of merchant’s wife.
Bride lets dagger fall and kill husband.
Bread accidentally dropped from tree on bear’s nose kills bear.
Man hidden in tree so frightened of lioness he drops his sword and kills her.
Man accidentally fed bread which his father has poisoned.
The wicked man puts poison in the bread he gives a beggar. The beggar gives his loaf to the son.
Poisoned bath prepared for another accidentally used by hero.
Horse accidentally poisoned instead of master.
An attempt is made to give the hero a poisoned cup. He is on horseback and spurs his horse away to avoid the cup. The poison is spilled and enters the horse’s ear and kills him.
Elephant on rampage accidentally poisoned instead of man.
Serpent carried by bird lets poison drop into milk and poisons drinkers.
Head of killed snake bites and kills king.
Snake in jug bites would-be thief.
Boy accidentally drinks “poison” intended for his stepbrother.
Doctor had substituted sleeping potion for the requested poison.
Youth accidentally takes the poison he intended for his father.
Man eats food which is mysteriously poisoned.
Hidden fruit accidentally poisoned by snake.
Aiming at fly has fatal results.
Person killed by hitting fly on his face.
To give child a slap to stop its crying, numskull kills it.
Man accidentally killed by bear trying to chase away flies.
Accidental fatal ending of game or joke.
Hanging in game or jest accidentally proves fatal.
Practical joker asks doctor to castrate him.
Unexpected death at hands of an animal.
Bird hunter killed by adder just as he is shooting bird.
Blood bath causes woman to be carried off by bird.
Sick queen lying under red satin carried off by bird who thinks it is red meat.
Ants gnaw a bowstring, so that the bow rebounds and cuts off head of man who is leaning on it.
Accidental death from flying splinter of bone.
Bone being gnawed by animal lets splinter fly and kills young animals.
Attacking animal is killed by another in ambush.
Tortoise lands on elephant’s back so that elephant’s back is broken.
Man dodging blow in dream hits his head against wall and kills himself.
Hero, while measuring wild boar, accidentally wounded mortally by bristle.
Axe thrown at one animal misses but kills another.
Death as result of mistaken identity: wrong person killed.
Saint changes places with charioteer; latter is killed.
Son killed because mistaken for someone else.
Father orders unrecognized son thrown into sea.
Man falls into jar of honey and is drowned.
Foxes crowd into house and are suffocated.
Groom killed by lightning on wedding night.
Uxorious king is burned to death while taking an alcohol bath.
Man forgets to wear magic gown and is killed.
Army drowned by unnoticed incoming tide.
Accidental death from fall on own weapon (shield).
Accidental death of father from fall into the fire when taking down weapons for his son.
Girl abducted by fairy left on shore, where she is accidentally drowned.
Youth gazing at own image reflected in water falls and drowns.
Girl lets down her sari for hero to climb up by but, when he is halfway up, sari breaks and he is killed.
Prefect, cursed by bishop, dies of fish-bone stuck in his throat.
Accidental death by striking head against lintel of door.
Wife throwing husband’s corpse into river (according to custom) is caught by corpse’s arm and drowned.
Thief crushed to death by fallen fragments of wall he has bored.
King mortally wounded on killed enemy’s tooth.
Bottle wherein jinn is imprisoned inadvertently opened and jinn escapes to kill his captor.
Suicide in remorse over hasty condemnation.
King hastily has 7,000 people put to death for stoning his judges to death.
Woman wrongly condemned for drunkenness when seen to take one drink.
Misunderstood message causes messenger to be killed (accused).
Hasty condemnation of man who accidentally becomes suspected of crime.
Faithful servant guarding master’s wife from danger falsely condemned for betraying his master.
Faithful son guarding his father from monster falsely accused by stepmother.
Stumbling over bloody corpse brings accusation of murder.
Jealous and overhasty man kills his rescuing twin brother.
False accusation overheard causes hasty killing.
Angry brother kills husband, thinking latter had killed wife (sister) and baby.
She is seen biting off finger of corpse to get its ring.
Lover kills self believing his mistress dead.
She has been frightened away by a lion.
Mistress kills self, believing her lover dead.
Woman feigns death to meet exiled lover.
It leads to his death. Lover hears of her supposed death, returns and submits to execution.
Lover commits suicide on finding beloved dead.
Father kills self believing that son is dead.
The son forgets to spread white sails, the prearranged signal of his safety.
Wrong sign put out leads to boys’ leaving home.
They are to be informed by a sign if a sister is born.
Father causes death of innocent son, believing him guilty of adultery with father’s wife.
An impoverished suitor has only a falcon to catch birds with. His lady’s sick son wants the falcon and she goes to ask for it. The suitor serves dinner for her
Pigeon hastily kills his mate for stealing wheat.
It has merely dried out and no longer fills the nest. When the dampness later swells the wheat, he sees his mistake and kills himself in remorse.
Innocent man accidentally suspected of crime.
Clerk who enters tavern arrested with others for murder.
Saint who entered house of ill fame to reform inmates accused of going with evil intent.
Boy is hanged for cattle theft; the strayed cattle are discovered later.
Man having purchased stolen ornament unwittingly presents it to owner as gift; is thrown into jail as thief.
Poor man presented rich robe by emperor is locked up as a thief.
Greedy disciple decides to remain in city despite learned teacher’s warning and is condemned to take the place of a thief.
Suspicions aroused when villain leaves his handkerchief in her room.
Warriors erroneously slay allies in night battle.
Father kills his son in battle rage.
King, seeing eldest son leaving room, decides that he is a rakshasa.
Unlucky man given a loaf which is filled with gold exchanges it for another loaf.
Boy’s servant takes pearl to his wife instead of to merchant; she throws it away.
Beggar accidentally overlooks money put into his way.
Bird carries off ring which lover has taken from sleeping mistress’s finger.
He searches for the ring and becomes separated from her.
Bird carries off jeweled veil with which girl had covered sleeping lover’s face.
Lover pursues bird and becomes separated from the girl.
Jewel (garment) carried off by bird from bather.
Clothes have been left on bank of stream.
Serpent steals jewels: person falsely accused of theft.
Boy unwittingly commits incest with his mother.
Man unwittingly falls in love with his own mother.
Father unwittingly falls in love with daughter.
Brother and sister unwittingly in love with each other.
Boy says, “Whoever eats this mushroom is my wife.”
His own sister eats it and he runs away.
Daughter unwittingly turns her own parents out of doors.
Drop of honey causes chain of accidents.
Ant pinching frog causes chain of accidents.
Fugitive slave takes wrong road and is caught.
Man falls dead from sudden realization.
Man falls dead when he realizes that he has been riding over frozen sea.
Man falls dead when he realizes that he has eaten bread from flour used for abscess plaster.
Mother dies of fright when she learns that she was about to commit incest with her son.
He has disguised himself to test her chastity.

Medical students (or student nurses or hospital employees) play trick on one of their number by suspending a cadaver arm or leg from the light cord in the person’s room (sometimes the object is placed in the person’s bed). Some circumstance keeps them from being on hand to observe the person’s reaction; the next day they remember the joke and go to the victim’s room to investigate. They have to break down the door. They find the victim sitting on the bed
Death in the graveyard; person’s clothing is caught; the person thinks something awful is holding him; he dies of fright.
Wicked stepmother falls into the fire because of fright.
Queen dies from fright because of evil prophecy.
Is frightened to death by the impersonation of demons.
Jester condemned to die on block. Pail of water used instead of axe.
Priest frightens boy by tying girl’s corpse to bell-rope.
In revenge the boy puts the body in the priest’s bed.
Lover frightens mistress as a joke.
Meaning to frighten son, father plays devil or a ghost. Son kills him.
Woman playing dead to spy on husband killed.
Brothers fall dead at sight of long lost brother whom they sold into captivity.
Person has successive misfortunes while making plans because he forgets to say, “If God wills.”
Lover’s wound breaks while he is in bed with mistress.
He bleeds to death (or is discovered because of the blood).
Lover’s spur catches in sheet when he tries to escape.
Man pinned in bed by weapon caught in quilt.
Quarrel over dog starts the Guelph-Ghibelline feud.
Blind men accidentally hurt each other.
Lover who is detained away beyond stipulated time returns to find fiancée married.
Hospitality enforced on hero keeps him overlong from home; meantime wife abducted.
Mistress expecting lover accidentally exchanges places with her maidservant.
Robber attempting to steal cow at night seizes thieving tiger.
Escaping prisoner falls by accident onto tiger’s back and is carried away.
Woman errs on to the road-of-the-tiger: carried off.
Delay in bringing pardon allows deserved execution.
Messenger, ignorant of contents of message, stops to view culprit’s execution.
Sign of prisoner’s reprieve changed by wind.
A flag to be flown in certain way, but wind catches it just at the wrong moment so that prisoner is executed.
Man blinded trying to heal girl.
Powders blow into his one good eye.
Watchman falls asleep as enemy approaches.
Mistake in interpreting prophecy (oracle) brings misfortune.
Shipwrecked man lands on deadly enemy’s territory and is attacked.
Man’s inordinate laughter brings unfortunate results.
Man discovers he is married to wer-tiger.
Object unknown in a country sold for a fortune.
A cat in a mouse-infested land without cats sold for a fortune.
Sickle sold for fortune in land without sickles.
Fortune from informing foreign king of use of saddle, bridle, and stirrups.
Salt in saltless land sold for fortune.
Sandalwood merchant sells his product at high price in land lacking sandalwood.
Fortune from trifling sum sent abroad with merchant.
The king buys shoes for a high price and then has all his dinner guests buy them.

Blotches on face of satirist (judge) as punishment for wrongful satire (judgment).
Judge must yield bench to son because he had made a false judgment.
Man promises more to church than he can possibly provide: punished.
Devil condemns rich man who does not repent until ready to die.
Woman on visit to world of dead may not return until she pays debt to dead.
Devil carries off rich man at death.
Avaricious man has neck broken when top of his treasure chest falls on him.
Avaricious miser tries to eat his adored money and chokes to death.
Avaricious woman and her gold consumed by hell’s fires which burn in her grave.
Dead usurer fed molten silver by devil.
Church built by usurer’s money made to collapse by devil.
Devils carry away stones of church built with ill-gotten money.
Use of false weights and measures punished.
Devils carry off girl who abuses her mother.
Girl cruel to her mother is slain by God.
Woman eats flesh and leaves cat only bones of fish cat has caught for them.
Ungrateful king raises old woman’s rent; miraculous punishment.
Irreverent young people punished by outraged old man.
Punishment for cutting off bird’s tongue.
Man slits tongue of magpie so that it can learn to speak.
His fingernails grow out like bird’s claws as punishment.
Boy reaches into bird’s nest for pigeon’s eggs.
A stone in the nest holds his hand for three days and nights. He is finally released by prayers.
Priest will not bury dead unless paid in advance.
Ruler has him buried alive with the corpse.
St. Peter’s mother dropped from heaven because of hardheartedness.
She is permitted to go to heaven on a stalk, but is weighted down by people holding to her skirts. She shakes them off.
Punishment of hard-hearted masters in other world.
Monkey destroys nest of bird who has made sport of him.
Sack of flour pushed down on peasant who accuses his wife of theft from it.
Three men find a purse. They are loath to pick it up, since they will have to divide. The king sees this and assigns them their proper punishments.
Punishment for finding fault with God’s works in heaven.
Punishment for finding fault with God’s forgiveness of sin.
Fault-finding with God’s handling of weather.
Women who will not sew are cast from community.
Devil torments old man who has laid aside his humility.
Devil impersonates woman’s maid at her toilette.
Vain woman has her cheeks miraculously burned.
Husband rubs off paint from wife’s cheeks.
Threatens to scrape them the next time.
Husband puts soot on wife’s cheeks to discourage her from using paint.
Vain woman wears corset so tight that it stifles her to death.
Clothes-proud woman trips over long skirt.
Jackal demands to be praised as god: runs with pack of hounds.
“God has no use for me, and the devil will not take me.”
On the way home the bold woman is strangled by the devil.
Request for immortality punished by transformation into tree.
A squire demands somebody to paint a living picture of the devil; when he sees it, he dies.
Devil punishes girl who loves to dance.
Freemasons forced to dance till they sweat blood.
Prince of devils gives up seat to man who goes to hell for singing worldly songs.
Punishment of evil magician who has caused plague.

Horse must break leg, since he has broken leg of man who broke leg of dog which bit leg of fox.
Punishment of children for parents’ offenses.
Punishment not meted out to persons below twenty years.

Punishment: winning as wife and then killing.

Undesired suitor killed asleep in his tent.
Death of father (son, etc.) as punishment.

Woman who disrobes to attract attention of hostile fighter killed.

Death as punishment for reproach concerning physical deformity (blemish).
Man killed because of scornful singing.

Hanging as punishment for stealing from a church.
Maidens slain in revenge for deaths of young men.
Charge of theft avenged by assault.
Death as punishment for spying on uncanny persons.
Death as punishment for dropping on emperor’s coat.
Punishment: millstone dropped on guilty person.
Impudent suitor or his messenger hanged or threatened with hanging.
Hanging as punishment for denying pagan gods.
Hanging as punishment for silence about hidden treasure.
Hanging by one foot as punishment for treachery.
Burning monastery and monks in it as punishment for incontinence.
Ravisher’s grave and body miraculously burnt.
Burning for traitor: unwittingly suggested by culprit.
Burning as punishment for betraying the confessional.
Woman saved from being burned as punishment for killing impudent suitor.
Boiling in tar as punishment for impostor.
Punishment: imprisonment in white-hot iron house.
Punishment: crushing in rice mill and scattering ashes.
Punishment: dancing to death in red-hot shoes.
Punishment: king hung between two fires.
Woman cast on husband’s funeral pyre as punishment.
Punishment: transformation to deer which is devoured by dogs.
Punishment: tying man to horses and setting vicious hounds after him.

Punishment: being fed to lions (wild beasts).

Heretic preaching against God’s creation worried to death by fly.

Quartering by horses as punishment for murder.
Quartering by horses as punishment for uxoricide.
Quartering by horses as punishment for impostor.

Punishment: dragging to death by a horse.
Punishment: drawing at the tails of horses.

Punishment: dropping and dashing to pieces.

Murder of faithless wife with poisoned salad.
Venomous snake put into the mouth as punishment for murder of newborn children.
Punishment by beheading and placing the heads on stakes.
Head cut off and hung on tree outside village.

Punishment for murder by fatal enema.

This given a lawyer who has “sold smoke”, i.e., idle words.

Heart and liver of son to be torn out.

Punishment: boring hot irons through ears.
Punishment: tearing off flesh with hot pincers.

Adulteress forced to have lover’s head before her at meals.

Punishment: eating ashes instead of food.
Punishment: eating ashes (coal) mixed with food.
Princess (queen) compelled to keep an inn.

Chained to a mountain with eagle preying on his vitals, which are restored nightly.
Lashed to a wheel which revolves continually.
Transformed to cow with gadfly ceaselessly pursuing.

Penance: killing oneself with wooden knife.

Penance: iron band forged round a man’s waist.

Penance: wearing friar’s cord about bare skin.

Penance: crawling to Rome on knees.
Penance: crawling to grave on knees.
Penance: walking on all-fours like beast.
Penance: eating food offered to dogs.
Penance: living under stairs as mendicant.

Refraining from sexual intercourse as penance.

Punishment: animal skin grows on man’s back.

Magic adhesion to object as punishment (for opposition to holy person).
Miraculous adhesion of objects to human hand as punishment for working on holy day.
Thief rendered unable to remove burden of stolen goods from his back.
Corpse of murdered man sticks to murderer’s back.

Magic sickness as punishment for theft.
Magic sickness as punishment for desecration of holy places (images, etc.).
Magic manifestation: blood flows suddenly from mouth of blasphemer.
Magic manifestation: eyes fall out of head of blasphemer.
Magic sickness (death) as punishment for inhospitality.

Magic paralysis as punishment for theft.
Magic paralysis as punishment for quarrelsomeness.
Deformity as punishment for false judging.

Punishment: grave fills with sand when digger attempts to bury sinner over holy man.

Drowning caused by magic wind as punishment of braggart.

Miraculous drowning as punishment for desire to murder.

Miraculous drowning as punishment for man’s flight with stepmother.

Punishment: being suspended between heaven and earth.

Punishment: angel ceases to appear to self-righteous hermit.

Sterility as punishment for breaking saint’s covenant.
Sterility as punishment for uncharitableness to holy person.
Painful birth of children as punishment.
Child taken from parents because they have ceased to think of God.

Failure in all efforts as punishment.
Rains withheld until king remembers to have monks’ huts roofed as promised.
Devil in roof of church into which he thrusts voices of loud singers.

Returning from the pope he is met by a mysterious animal who jumps on his back. Then in the man’s room, whither he has carried the animal, a three hours’ noise is heard as of a fight. Neither man nor beast is found in the room.
Cheaters visited by god in animal form.

Punishment for incest: father and son maddened; cut off their sexual organs.
Voice from heaven pronounces curse of destruction on city.
Permanent mark as curse on a murderer.

Makes away with the receipts of a merchant who had watered his wine.
Mouse causes hair of thief to fall out.

Object stolen (left) as token that infidelity has been discovered.
Husband leaves wooden sword in scabbard of wife’s paramour upon discovering their infidelity.
Husband and wife (king and queen) each unfaithful to other.
Man ejected from heaven for folly of marrying twice.
Christ, not having married, knew nothing about suffering.
So thinks the man after hearing all about Christ’s torments.
Man reprimanded by judge for marrying several times.
The man replies that he was always looking for a good wife.

The devil frightened by the shrewish wife. A man persuades his shrewish wife to let herself be lowered into a well. When he comes to pull her out he raises a genie (devil) who is glad to escape from the woman. Later he frightens the devil by telling him that his wife has escaped.
Devil flees shrewish wife and enters body of a duke.
Exorcised by telling him that they are sending for his wife.
Late husband chooses to remain in Purgatory rather than to return to his shrewish wife.
Husband chooses to go to hell rather than join shrewish wife in heaven.
Man in hell declares that life there is much better than on earth with his wife.
Man had rather remain transformed to mule than to live with his shrewish wife.
Man forces devil to take back the shrewish wife.
Minstrel throws wife into sea: her tongue the heaviest thing on board.
Ordered to throw all heavy articles overboard.
Thief overhears and oversees quarrel of two jealous wives.
Arraigned before judge, he asks any punishment be given him rather than that of having two wives.
By outdoing his wife in shrewishness the husband renders her obedient.
Shrew tamed by setting another shrew against her.
Husband dons armor and forces the household to shout: “Long live the Master!” Takes off his breeches and dares his wife to put them on.
Establishes his mastery in the home.
Wife becomes obedient on seeing husband slay a recalcitrant horse.
Husband tries to reform wife by killing a recalcitrant horse in her presence.
She thinks he has lost his mind and continues in her ways.
While asleep she is made to exchange places with the cobbler’s wife. She thinks she is in hell. The cobbler teaches her to obey and fear her husband.
Shrewish wife driven from home but when in danger, runs to husband and receives protection.
She is a good wife thereafter.
St. Peter’s wife meets him with a broom handle.
She is waiting for him at the rear door of the house.
He thus remarks as she empties slops on his head.
Strength in words, in herbs, and in stones.
When first two do not cure shrewish wife, the last does.
The browbeaten husband from under the table: “The man always has a man’s heart.”
Husband will not search for shrewish wife who has run away from him.
Shrewish wife gives husband heating every morning.
Husband consoled by seeing woman even more shrewish than his wife.
Wife beats her husband and eats up everything he earns.
Fakir thankful for shrewish wife: she is a thorn in his flesh and warns him from neglecting the ways of righteousness.
Unsuccessful search for man who can rule his wife.
Cock shows browbeaten husband how to rule his wife.
King sees how male stork kills his unfaithful wife.
Monkey (jackal, etc.) shows husband how to rule his wife.
King tells jackal his statistics are wrong since there are more men than women.
Wife threatens husband with death if he will not tell secrets.
Prize for husband who rules his wife.
Man claims prize (boots) as ruler of his house, but is afraid to carry the boots lest he soil his clean shirt and anger his wife.
Men rulers in their house asked to sing.
No man in congregation does so. Priest alone sings. Next year he cannot, for then he has a maid.
Wife threatens suicide if she does not have her own way.
Vexed woman brings pot down on husband’s head in presence of guest.
Nagging wife drives husband to prepare for suicide.
Woman advised that nagging will never make a husband virtuous.
Saint composes hymn to free himself from the mala vita in which he lives with his wife.
The husband shows his wife poison to avoid: she takes it and dies.
Husband forbids wife to ride on the dog: she immediately does so and is bitten.
Man with obedient wife looks young; with disobedient, old.
Man forbids wife to open chest.
Loaded crossbow placed in it. She opens it and is killed.
Husband warns wife not to enter empty furnace.
She does so and it falls in upon her.
Wife refuses to bring husband warm water: is beaten.
The obstinate wife: cutting with knife or scissors.
At the end of the argument the man throws his wife into the water. As she sinks she makes with her finger the motion of shearing with the scissors.
The obstinate wife sought for up-stream.
When she falls into the stream, the husband concludes that she would be too obstinate to go with the current.
The obstinate wife: sign of the louse.
She calls her husband a lousy head. He throws her into the stream. As she sinks she makes a sign of cracking a louse.
The obstinate wife: the third egg.
The husband and the wife dispute as to who shall eat the third egg. She pretends to die. At the grave she asks him, “Do I eat two of the three eggs?” and he gives his consent.
The obstinate wife: insists on eating three of the five eggs.
The dish which the husband detests and the wife keeps serving him.
He affects to like it and thus gets rid of it.
Obstinate wife refuses to take cover off boiling kettle.
Man warns his wife that he has dreamed that she is attacked by a wolf.
She pays no heed to him and the dream comes true.
Quarrel between husband and wife explained by their having been previously a tiger and a dog.
Quarrelsome wife conquered by silent husband.
Medicine against quarrelling: the wife must take one dose and keep it in her mouth for ten minutes as soon as her husband is angry.
Quarrelsome wife reproved by a good whipping.
Woman jealous of a fair maid in her house.
Fears her attraction for her husband.
King’s wives jealous of his attention to pet animal.
Wife exposes bald head of second wife to disgrace her.
Jealous wife (mistress) transforms rival to hound.
Decision not to punish a jealous husband: he already suffers enough.
Husband jealous of wife who goes to confession is punished by the priest.
When the husband sees the priest take her behind the altar to punish her he volunteers to take the punishment. The wife says, “Pound him well.
Jealous husband kills nightingale which his wife gets up to hear.
Woman’s scented hair attracts deer: husband jealous.
Jealous king causes massacre of handsome young captives.
Husband’s unjust jealousy forces wife to commit adultery.
Wife repays husband’s supposed adultery by doing likewise.
Jealous husband objects to wife’s enjoyment of intercourse: thinks she has had previous experience.
Jealous husband spends all his earnings as skillful smith bribing courtiers not to talk to his wife, and at last locks her up in hut in the forest.
Trickster sends jealous wife after husband: steals food.
Jealous wife ties husband to her so that he cannot get away to meet another woman.
The curious wife: wait and see.
A man and his wife overhear thieves planning to rob the house, put the man out of the way, and have their will of the wife. The man wants to raise an alarm.
Husband insists on knowing wife’s secret.
Wife insists upon knowing husband’s secret.
Husband takes wife’s place and receives punishment for her adultery.
Shows what she has done for her husband, but not what she has done for herself.
She shows her children as her jewels.
Beautiful woman married to hideous man: he is thankful, she patient.
She says that they have thus both gained paradise.
Woman gets rid of impotent husband and remarries.
Mistress of impotent husband sends her maid to find a man for her.
Silent wife brought to speech by dangers to her husband.
Host gives his wife (daughter) to his guest as bed companion.
Handmaid given as wife unto husband by barren wife.
First (barren) wife insists her husband should take second wife.
Wife withholds intercourse from husband to enforce demand.
Frightened wife shows marks of affection for husband.
This is so rare that he pardons the robber who has caused the fright.
Mistress has always said her “Aves”: Virgin Mary refuses to help wife against her rival.
The wife tells this to the mistress, who repents.
Sight of mistress’s ring causes husband to withhold himself from his wife.
Why separation of a good woman from a bad man is a benefit.
Wife refuses to sleep with detested husband.
Wife curses unbeloved husband who attempts to force her.
Wife keeps vow never to wed after her husband’s death.
Husband (wife) of supernatural being longs for old home and visits relatives.
Husband’s indiscreet boast about wife brings about his death.

King regards his wife as so beautiful that he has a friend view her naked through a crack in the wall. Wife learns of his act, goes over to the man who has viewed her, and with the latter brings about the king’s death.
Wife buys (sells) privilege of sleeping one night with husband.
Sleeping with head laid in wife’s lap as sign of tenderness.
Wife gives wise warning to husband.
Man warned by wife against stepping on red cloth.
Wife warns departing hero against seductions of women.
“Night of Sabbath” (Friday night) only devoted to conjugal pleasures.
Woman’s aversion to marriage motivated through a dream.
Flight of maiden (bridegroom) to escape marriage.
Woman prefers to remain chaste rather than keep an impotent husband.
Girl commits suicide rather than marry man she does not love.
Girl remains a virgin after both her suitors are killed in battle.
Maiden queen prefers to fight instead of marrying, but is at last conquered and married.
Woman dies when spoiled of her sanctity.
Ravished girl’s virginity restored by Virgin Mary.
Ravished girl’s virginity restored by saint.
Pregnant nun’s virginity restored through power of saint.
Father kills daughter lest she become prostitute.
Father kills daughter lest she become the property of a tyrant.
The audacious water and the continent husband.
A woman with a continent husband (lover) splashes water on her thighs as she crosses a stream and then reproves it for being bolder than her husband. She thus calls attention to her situation.
Wife reproves continent husband by showing conduct of cock and hens.
Wife reforms continent husband by having walls of bedroom painted with erotic scenes.
Woman continent in two marriages to become a nun.
Repression of lust through sitting in water.
Man and woman in chaste love for twenty-five years.
Monk finds that only abuse and cruel treatment from his fellow monks can conquer his lust.
Had substituted for husband’s mistress. Proves legitimacy of her child by producing tokens and by child’s missing toe (like her husband’s four-toed foot).
Repeated attempts to seduce innocent woman. She escapes them all.
Virginity saved in spite of torture.
Girl kills man who threatens her virtue.
Woman escaping from slavery kills man who would ravish her.
Bride puts to flight man who attempts to ravish her.
Widow dons late husband’s armor to put would-be ravisher to flight.
Wife escapes lust of king by shaming him.
Woman escapes king’s lust by inducing bad breath.
Girl gives up wealth and flees to escape lecherous emperor.
Wife sets fire to house to escape undesired lover.
Escape from undesired lover by miracle.
Maid pledged to celibacy is given, at her prayer, a beard.
Girl named Mary has virginity spared by knight who has bought her.
Girl’s virginity spared by knight when he sees her surrounded by the Virgin and her train.
In her straits the girl has prayed for help.
Girl prays to Virgin to spare her virginity.
Two soldiers quarrel over possessing her. Captain slays her, thus “saving” her.
Magic sickness (discomfort) prevents lover from raping woman.
In answer to maiden’s prayer saint changes boat’s course and guides it to another place.
Girl strikes man who tries to kiss her.
Woman kicks lecherous monk down the stairs.
Princess threatens to kill amorous king.
Undesired lover drugged and carried out.
Girl pleads vow of chastity to repel lover.
Escape from undesired lover by strategy.
Princess escapes from undesired lover by fleeing disguised as a bishop.
Princess evades unwelcome lover by putting on foul-smelling skin-coat.
Girl’s virginity saved by the kindness of an emissary.
Makes the lord believe she is a relative.
Chaste woman resists advances of a conqueror.
Chaste woman promises conqueror drug of invulnerability.
Girls drown selves to save their virginity.
Man is killed defending sweetheart’s honor.
Maiden sends to her lecherous lover (brother) her eyes (hands, breasts) which he has admired.
Woman successfully prays for disease to repel lover.
Saint plucks out her eye when urged to marry.
Maidens befoul selves with blood to escape rape.
Woman raises sores on her body to preserve chastity.
Princess takes on loathsome disguise to avoid unwelcome demon-lover.
Girl escapes from undesired lover by cutting off her plaits of hair.
Girl lives in sepulchre to preserve chastity.
Knight unsuccessfully tempted by host’s wife.
Woman masks as man to deceive anchorite.
No place secret enough for fornication.
When he is about to give in to temptation a dove flies out of his mouth. On repenting the dove re-enters his mouth.
Saint flogs woman who tempts him.
Saint sleeps with maidens without sinning.
Another saint, who doubts fact, undergoes same test and perceives its efficacy.
Monk unsuccessfully tempted by woman he formerly loved.
When she seeks him in his bed he screams. He says she steals his most valuable possession, virtue.
Man tempted by fiend in woman’s shape.
Woman sent by deity to tempt self-righteous anchorite.
Man mutilates himself to remove temptation.
Tempted man bites out his tongue and spits it in temptress’s face.
Tempted man burns off his fingers.
Man disfigures his face to remove temptation.
Tempted rabbi tears out his eyes to escape temptation.
Hero cuts off head and wraps it in napkin so he will not be tempted by sight of virgins.
Monk cures himself of desire for dead sweetheart.
Monk goes into desert to avoid temptation of women, the prime source of sin.
Saint exposes self to temptation but preserves chastity.
Thus insures self greater reward in Heaven.
Sight or touch of woman as source of sin.
Woman’s girdle as source of sin.
Woman’s voice as source of sin.
Woman wagers that she can seduce anchorite.
Saint’s enemy, wishing to cause saint to violate his oath never to “commit folly and utter lie,” induces his daughter to tempt saint.
Saint perceives trick and avoids sin.
Ascetic successfully tempted: kills son born in consequence.
A two-edged sword is laid between the couple sleeping together.
Boy sleeps between couple to safeguard their virtue.
Object set between beds of couple sleeping in same room.
Chaste sleeping together to torment woman.
Chaste sleeping together with six sisters-in-law one by one.
Young man sleeps on girl’s mat without touching her to signify his desire.
Nun refuses to look at man.
Nun so opposed to seeing men that she refuses to see St. Martin.
The boy who had never seen a woman: the Satans.
When he sees a girl and asks his father what it is, the father tells him it is Satan.
Boy is denied sight of all women except his mother and his nurse until he is eighteen.
He falls in love with the first woman who is more attractive than his mother.
Adulterous love changed into a chaste one.
Heavy chastity belt imposed on wife.
Man puts marriage ring on finger of statue of Venus (Virgin Mary). She afterwards forbids him the embraces of an earthly bride.
Man leaves earthly bride for service of Virgin.
Imprisoned virgin to prevent knowledge of men (marriage, impregnation).
Girl intended for marriage with king cloistered.
Wife imprisoned in tower (house) to preserve chastity.
Guarded maiden first seen by hero in church.
Guarded maiden first seen by hero in otherworld.
Attempt to keep wife chaste by carrying her in box.
In spite of all precautions she meets men.
Other futile attempts to keep wife chaste.
Message of chastity: uncooked meat left behind.
Man conducting a woman leaves uncooked meat behind each night of the journey as a sign to the husband following that she has not been touched.
Virgin Mary as protectress of illicit lovers.
Pregnant abbess secretly delivered of her child by Virgin Mary.
Master discovers that slave girl he wants to marry is a near relative.
Unnatural father wants to marry his daughter.
Father by trickery secures priest’s advice to marry his own daughter.
If a man raise a lamb, shall he eat it himself or let another eat it?
Father feigning death returns in disguise and seduces daughter.
Girl got with child by intoxicated father.
Mother guilty of incest with son forgiven by Pope (Virgin Mary).
Incognito son tempts mother to see whether all women are wicked.
Mother guilty of incest with son whose honor she is testing.
Boy courts his mother, is driven off by father.
Lovers reared as brother and sister learn to their joy that they are not related.
Two lovers give each other up when they learn that they are brother and sister.
When boy cannot have his sister for a wife he asks for one of her eyes and ears instead.
Youth attempts to seduce his grandmother.
Husband unable to change her ways, submits to them.
Woman disappointed in love threatens to become prostitute.
Devil causes girl to become prostitute.
Destroys the girl’s family and begets on her a boy.
Mother acts as procuress of bedmate for her son.
Getting advice from a woman in bed.
Hero learns feats of arms through gratifying woman’s lust.
Woman sells favors for particular purpose.
Woman sells favors to obtain a jewel.
Woman sells favors to obtain many jewels.
Woman sacrifices her honor to free her husband (brother) from prison.
Woman commits adultery to obtain aid for husband in battle.
Woman sells favors for beautiful clothes.
Women sells favors for new shoes.
Parents urge girl to trade her favors for truce with hostile warrior.
Woman gives favors to pay for help across river.
Woman sells favors for large sum of money (property).
Princess gives herself to Turks of her own accord in order to save her people.
Bed-partner to receive payment from first man she meets in the morning.
Girl dares not receive gift from a man as it may be supposed to be payment for her favors.
Woman enjoys the ravishings of the enemy.
Women cohabit with magic house pillars.
Lesbian love: women give birth to monsters as result.
Intercourse of a human being and an animal.
Sheep born with human head as a result of bestiality.
Foal born of Loki after dealing with mythical stallion.
Homocentaurus born as a result of bestiality.
Children are spotted like leopards as result of bestiality.
Pig born with head like that of man as a result of bestiality.
Necrophilism: sexual intercourse with dead human body.
Man unwittingly ravishes his own sister.
Wild man as ravisher of women.
Husband sends wife poison to avoid having her ravished by the enemy.
Unknown paramour discovered by string clue.
Hero lies by princess in magic sleep and begets child.
King’s mistress secretly becomes hero’s without revealing identity.
Adulteress roughly treated by her lover.
Queen’s illicit passion for diseased man.
Queen commits adultery with low-born man.
Adulteress sells self to devil for money.
King takes subject’s wife while her husband is sent away.
Queen begets son with duke while the king is in war.
Woman advises husband to kill guest else, she will make him chase husband and marry her instead.
Maidservant given to lover’s companion as bed-partner.
Fruit-picking time used for sexual promiscuity.
Man has a son not his wife’s; wife has a daughter not her husband’s.
Queen makes all men who come to serve her copulate with her.
Black nipples of girl’s breasts reveal her loss of virginity.

Red rose brings boy, white rose a girl.
Conception from swallowing worm (in drink of water).
Conception from eating parts of human being.
Conception after eating honey given by lover.
Conception from eating mess of fairy pottage.
Woman impregnated after accidentally partaking of crane’s dung.
Conception from drinking elixir from goat’s horns.
Conception after reciprocal desire for each other.
Conception after anchorite blesses woman in love with him.
Conception from rays of a dragon.
Magic impregnation by use of charm (amulet).
Conception from casual contact with man.
Conception from having licked semen-stained loincloth.
Conception from contact with magic object.
Conception by smell of cooked dragon heart.
Conception from stepping on an animal.
Conception from fruit thrown against breast.
Conception from flowers hidden in breast.
Cow touched by arrow becomes pregnant.
Conception from putting on another’s girdle.
Conception from putting ball into bosom.
Woman becomes pregnant after eagle sits on her head.
Conception after shadow of man has fallen on bathing girl.
Conception from feathers falling on woman.
Hero enters womb of sleeping woman and is reborn.
Heifers covered by supernatural bull conceive miraculously.
Birth from unusual part of person’s body.
Boy created by saint from blood-clot.
Birth from wound or abscess on body of father.
Child born of splinter in hand (foot).
Birth from secretions of the body.
Birth from mucus from the nose.
Birth from contact of severed male genitals with ground.
Birth from semen thrown on ground.
Birth from lotus issuing from a god’s navel.
Birth of human being from an egg.
Shepherdess born of red and blue egg.
Twig, born of a woman, is planted and becomes a girl.
Birth obtained through magic or prayer.
Child born in answer to prayer.
Hateful or lovely child to be born first?
Magic rites for obtaining a child.
Magic elixir to procure a child.
Charity rewarded by birth of child.
Vegetable comes to life at woman’s prayer.
Fish when slit open gives up baby boy.
Abnormally born child has unusual powers.
Monstrous birth because mother sees horrible sight.
Blemished children born of monstrous parent.
Only half a son is born by queen who ate merely half of mango.
Poor woman gives birth to child who has no body (merely head or skull).
Child born as formless lump of flesh.
Monstrous birth: child with donkey’s head.
Boy born with one side flesh and one iron.
Child born beautiful on one side, hairy on other.
Child born half man, half fish.
Child born with claws as result of curse by dying peddler murdered by its parents.
Monstrous birth—nine faces, nine arms, nine feet.
Child with all of its organs out of place.
Girl born with red string around neck.
Child born with snake around neck.
Child born bearing lizard in each hand.
Child born holding worm (in each hand).
Child born carrying knife and calabash.
Child born carrying handful of hair.
Child born with magic iron bow.
Child born with knife and shield.
Daughter born with a feathered parka.
Thumbling born as result of hasty wish of parents.
They wish for a child, no matter how small he may be.
Woman transformed to animal bears animal.
Tiger, spirit, and man sons of one mother.
Woman gives birth to a snake.
Woman gives birth to a bird.
Supernaturally impregnated woman gives birth to dragon.
Woman gives birth to a plant.
Woman gives birth to a fruit.
Queen gives birth to a gourd.
Woman gives birth to a demon.
Child born with viper in heart (body).
Child of three fathers born with three stripes.
Child formed of clot of gore has red birthmark.
Child born with figure of serpent on his body.
Tattoo on newly born baby’s back telling who was his former incarnation.
Queen delivered of a piece of flesh; abandoned and saved, it gradually separates into forms of boy and girl.
Mother sits on stone to prevent premature birth.
Hero an abortion thrown into the bushes.
Woman conceives and bears same day.
Delayed by an enemy who bewitches the mother.
Child in mother’s womb reveals crime.
Child in mother’s womb reveals murder.
Child in mother’s womb reveals adultery.
Child in mother’s womb reveals unjust judgment.
Future suicide weeps in mother’s womb.
Twins quarrel before birth in mother’s womb.
Future poet chants spell in mother’s womb.
Children in mothers’ wombs praise God at birth of Christ.
Embryos in womb join melody and sing.
Child in mother’s belly guides her.
Unborn child directs his mother on journey.
Woman talks to her child before it is conceived.
Child speaks from dead mother’s womb.
Child in mother’s womb visible from outside.
Fetus exchanged from one woman to another.
Male embryo transformed in womb to female.
Man transformed to female (human or animal) bears offspring.
Sheath and knife as analogy for mother and unborn child.
Girl’s blood examined to see if she is pregnant.
Mother of saint has healing spittle during pregnancy.
Saint performs miracles while yet unborn.
Worm swallowed at conception eats hand of babe before birth.
King demands that his pregnant queen be chained to him.
Girl betrays pregnancy by dropping milk on brother.
Jewess must entreat Virgin before she can bear her child.
Child born of woman abandoned in pit.
Child born to an apparently dead mother in her grave.
Blind wives fall into a pool where they give birth to children.
Woman bears twins at end of footrace (with king’s horses).
Twins born in tent; mother abducted.
Boy is born in a wrapping of fine cloth.
Avoidance of evil spirits at childbirth.
All locks in house to be shot during childbirth.
Knots to be untied at childbirth.
Particularly knots in the woman’s clothes.
Knife (other sharp instrument) as childbirth precaution.

Child removed from body of dead mother.

Twins freed from dead mother’s body as body rots.
Cesarean operation upon a woman at childbirth as a custom.
Piglings cut from bodies of sows and reared.
Prolonged labor: woman has childbirth pains for 100 days but is not delivered.

Child helps mother in severing his navel string.
Child stronger than mother on day of birth.
Child speaks prematurely on first birthday.

Extraordinary number of children in family.
Multiple birth as result of relations with several men.

Triplets killed by tribe at birth.

Four calves to one cow at a birth.

Spring forth as hero is born; act as life tokens, etc.

Abandoned child saved by seagulls; milk furnished by doe; angel brings bell as drinking utensil.
